Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 1:

After the surah of al-Nur ended with this verse, ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He already knows your condition. And the Day they are returned to Him, He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [24:64], which shows what Allah, exalted is He, possesses of dominion, subjugation and sovereignty, and showed that the return to Him and the coming back on the Day of Resurrection is for reckoning, the surah of al-Furqan begins to show that this dominion is not a dominion of enslavement, but a dominion of mercy. He has arranged life for you so that you may live in it upon guidance and light. So He, exalted is He, said:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [25:1].

﴿Blessed...﴾ [25:1] (al-Furqan): The root b-r-k customarily indicates blessing, which is that a thing gives you good beyond what you expected of it and exceeds your estimate, as when you are shown food for three and it suffices ten. So you say: this food is blessed, or it has blessing in it.

Among the meanings of tabāraka (be blessed) is: His measure is exalted, and ﴿Blessed...﴾ [25:1] (al-Furqan): He is transcendent above the likeness of anything other than Him, and tabāraka: His goodness and His giving are magnified. You will find these three complementing one another.

Remarkable is that this word ﴿Blessed...﴾ [25:1] (al-Furqan) is miraculous in its orthography and miraculous in its derivation. If you trace the Qur'an you will find that this word occurs in the Qur'an nine times: seven of them with an alif, and two without the alif (1). Why was it not written with the alif in all, or without it in all? That is to demonstrate that the orthography of the Qur'an is tawqīfī (divinely prescribed), not a mechanical matter, as in His saying, exalted is He, at the beginning of surah al-‘Alaq: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾ [96:1], where the word ism is written here with an alif, and in the rest of the Qur'an without the alif.

Therefore: the Qur'an is not ordinary in its orthography and writing, and not ordinary in its recitation. You read any other book in whatever state you are, but for the Qur'an you must be in wudu' and approach it in purity... and so on, of what we know of the etiquette of Qur'an recitation.

As for derivation, we know that the verb derives a past, a present, an imperative, an active participle, and so on. But ﴿Blessed..﴾ [25:1] (al-Furqan): the Qur'an mentions from it only this form, as though He wishes to reserve it for the transcendence of Allah, exalted is He, like the word subḥān (glory be). Therefore, despite how many tyrants throughout history forced people to praise them and submit to them, we have never seen anyone, however criminal in religion, say to one of them: subḥānaka.

Therefore we say in glorifying Allah: subḥānaka, and it is not said except to You, however much the atheists dare, they do not utter it to other than Allah.

Thus: ﴿Blessed...﴾ [25:1] (al-Furqan) revolves around three meanings: His measure is exalted, He is transcendent above resembling anything other than Him, and His goodness and giving are magnified. And among the magnitude of His goodness, glory be to Him, is that He has no like: in His measure, nor in His essence, nor in His attributes, nor in His acts. And all of this is for our own benefit, for there is no Great but Allah, no Compeller but Allah, and no Rich but Allah.

The Qur'an was named al-Furqan because it distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and the Qur'an was sent down to bring people out of darknesses into light, so that people walk upon guidance and insight. The Qur'an, then, is a criterion that distinguishes for them the places of good from the places of ruin. So al-Furqan operates in all directions of religion: in religion there is a summit, which is the Truth, Blessed and Exalted is He, and a conveyor from the summit, who is the Messenger (ﷺ), and those to whom he is sent, who are the believers. So the Qur'an came to distinguish truth from falsehood in these three.

At the summit, there were those who denied the existence of a Creator God of this universe, and others who say there are multiple gods, and both are at opposite extremes from each other; there is no current of thought uniting them. So the Qur'an came to distinguish truth from falsehood in this matter, and says: the matter is a middle course between what you have said: God exists, but He is one God with no partner. Thus it made a distinction on the question of the summit.

Likewise it made a distinction on the question of his being a human from his people. When some of them objected to him and envied him this rank, though he was one of them, Allah strengthened him with the miracle that supports him and manifests his truthfulness in conveying from Allah. His miracle (ﷺ) was in a thing in which the people excelled, namely eloquence, rhetoric and clear expression, and the Arabs are people of expression; this was their current merchandise, and he challenged them with this miracle and they were unable.

Likewise it made a distinction on the question of creation with respect to the foundations of their life. It explained to them the lawful and the unlawful. As for the preservation of the species, it explained to them the lawful, prescribed marriage for them, and forbade them from fornication, to preserve the lineage of the vicegerent of Allah on earth.

Thus: the Qur'an made a distinction in everything: in the God, in the Messenger, and in the foundations of the life of those to whom he is sent. And since it has made a distinction in all these matters, there is no word better than that we name it "al-Furqan."

There is no doubt that the words through which the Truth, Blessed and Exalted is He, speaks have radiances, and within them are meanings known to people of reflection and insight whom Allah has opened [His understanding] to. How alike they are to diamond gems! What makes the diamond precious is that in each of its atoms there are radiant refractions found in nothing else; from whatever side you look at it, a reflected ray meets you giving a sparkle and luster that glitters from all its sides. Likewise are the words of the Noble Qur'an.

Among the meanings of al-Furqan, some scholars said it was sent down in separate parts, as in His saying: ﴿And a Qur'an We have separated, that you may recite it to the people over a long period, and We have sent it down progressively﴾ [17:106]. That is: We sent it down in parts; it was not sent down once like the books before it. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has wisdom in sending the Qur'an in parts, as it gives the opportunity for each portion of the Qur'an that descends to be absorbed by people, because it is tied to a particular event, and likewise so that the required gradualness in legislation takes place.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And a Qur'an We have separated, that you may recite it to the people over a long period, and We have sent it down progressively﴾ [17:106].

The early Muslims during the period of the Qur'an's revelation were much given to questions, asking the Messenger of Allah about matters of religion, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They ask you about the crescent moons﴾ [2:189], ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ [2:219], ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ [8:1]. So a portion of the Qur'an would descend to answer them and legislate for them, and this would not have been possible had the Qur'an descended all at once.

The phrase ﴿sent down the Criterion﴾ [25:1] supports and reinforces this meaning, because "nazzala" indicates the repetition of the action, unlike "anzala," which indicates the action occurring once.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿upon His servant﴾ [25:1]: it is as though the ground of the sending down is servanthood to Allah, exalted is He; he is the servant whom the Qur'an was entrusted to be sent down upon. We have already said that servanthood is a hateful term if it is used on any side other than the Truth, glory be to Him; but servanthood to Allah is honor and nobility, and a beloved term in the servanthood of creatures to the Creator, because servanthood to people means the master takes the best of his servant, whereas servanthood to Allah means the servant takes the best of his Master.

Therefore Allah, exalted is He, made servanthood to Him the ground for elevation to heaven in the Night Journey, so He said: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾ [17:1]. So the elevation here came from servanthood to Allah.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [25:1]. "The worlds" (al-'alamīn): the plural of "'alam" (world), and "'alam" is everything other than Allah, exalted is He. Among the worlds: the world of the angels, the world of mankind, the world of jinn, the world of animals, the world of plants, the world of inanimate matter. However, some of these worlds have not been reached by a bringer of good news or a warner, because they are not endowed with choice, and good news and warning are only for one who has choice.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it; but man bore it. Indeed, he was ever unjust and ignorant﴾ [33:72].

So if you exclude from these worlds those who have no choice, what remains are the jinn and mankind, and to them the Messenger (ﷺ) was sent as a bringer of good news and a warner. But why did He say here ﴿that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [25:1] and not say "a bringer of good news and a warner"?

They said: because He, glory be to Him, will speak here about those who plunged into matters of divinity, and for those warning is fitting rather than good news. Therefore He says in the verse after it: ﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has not taken a son, and has not had a partner in the dominion, and created everything and determined it with precise determination﴾ [25:2].

1 - ﴿Blessed﴾ occurs in seven places with an alif: (al-A'raf: 54), (al-Mu'minun: 14), (al-Furqan: 1, 10, 21), (Ghafir: 64), (al-Zukhruf: 85).
- It occurs twice without the alif ﴿Blessed﴾: (al-Rahman: 78), (al-Mulk: 1). Al-Suyuti said in (al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an) (2/188): "Tabaraka: a verb that is used only in the past tense, and is used only for Allah."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 2:

At the end of Surah al-Nur, He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Verily, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth... [24:64]﴾. There He mentioned the ownership of what is contained (al-mazruf), whereas here He said: ﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth... [25:2]﴾. Here He mentioned the ownership of the container (al-zarf), that is, the heavens and the earth.

Then He, glory be to Him, spoke about the great falsehood that they dared to utter, saying: ﴿and He has not taken a son, and He has no partner in the dominion... [25:2]﴾.

We have previously spoken at length about the matter of taking a son and its wisdom. People love children either so that they may be an extension of one's remembrance, or so that they may support their father in his weakness, or for multiplying (their number). But Allah, blessed and exalted is He, is the Living who does not die, who has no need of anyone to perpetuate His remembrance, and He is the Strong who has no need of other than Himself. Why, then, would He take a son?

As for His saying: ﴿and He has no partner in the dominion... [25:2]﴾, this is a matter confirmed by reality. For Allah, exalted is He, was the first to bear witness, and He bore witness to Himself, saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge [also bear witness]... [3:18]﴾.

That is: when the angels were created, they bore witness to Allah, exalted is He; then those of knowledge bore witness through reasoning and inference. So the witness of the Truth, glory be to Him, to Himself is the witness of the Essence to the Essence; the angels witnessed by direct observation (mushahadah), and we witness by inference and proof (istidlal and burhan).

Blessed and exalted is the Truth, who gives us the evidence for the veracity of this observation, and He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Allah has not taken any son, nor was there with Him any deity; otherwise each deity would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overcome others... [23:91]﴾.

And He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Say: If there were with Him other deities, as they say, they would surely have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne [17:42]﴾.

This is the logical, sound reasoning with which we refute these people: if there were other deities with Allah, each of them would have taken a part of the universe and made it his own private domain, and each would have exalted himself over the others and fought against him. And if there were other deities with Him, glory be to Him, they would have gathered against the one who seized the dominion from them, to judge him or to seek his intercession.

We have said that a claim is established for its claimant when no one else claims it for himself, and this matter has not been claimed by anyone; therefore it is established for Allah, exalted is He, until there appears someone who claims this creation for himself.

We have previously given an example of this with a group of people in a gathering, one of whom lost his wallet there. When they had left, the owner of the house found it and asked them about it, but none of them claimed it. Then one of them contacted him, saying: "It is mine." There is no doubt that it belongs to him until another claimant appears, and then we decide between them.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿and He created everything and determined it with precise measure [25:2]﴾. The creation of Allah, exalted is He, is not haphazard; rather He created it with measure, reckoning and wisdom, so He creates each thing according to the measure of the task it performs. Therefore He said in another place: ﴿Who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided [87:2-3]﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 3:

﴿And they have taken, besides Him, gods who create nothing, while they themselves are created, and who control neither harm nor benefit for themselves, nor control death, nor life, nor resurrection.﴾

That is: they have brought gods other than God. These gods, by their own admission, their testimony and their reality, create nothing. Yet it is not merely that they create nothing; they themselves are created. Thus two matters are combined in them.

This is one of the verses at which the orientalists paused, saying that it contains an apparent contradiction, because God, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿So blessed is God, the best of creators﴾ (al-Mu'minun). Here He affirmed that there are others with Him who have the attribute of creating, as proven by His joining them with Himself, while He is the best of them. In another place He, glorified be He, says: ﴿And [make him] a messenger to the Children of Israel: "I have certainly come to you with a sign from your Lord: that I will create for you from clay like the form of a bird, then I will breathe into it and it will be a bird by permission of God..."﴾ (Al 'Imran).

In reply to these, we say: come, let us first understand the meaning of creation (khalq). Creation is the bringing into existence of that which did not exist, as we previously illustrated by the making of a glass cup from the melting of certain materials. The cup did not exist, and he brought it into existence, but from a pre-existing thing; and the cup remains fixed in its state. But the Truth, glorified and exalted, brings into existence from non-existence: non-existence from non-existence, and He brings it into a form in which there is life, growth and reproduction from its own self, as He, glorified be He, said: ﴿And of all things We created pairs that you might remember﴾ (adh-Dhariyat).

Those who now manufacture artificial roses, and strive hard to imitate the natural rose which He created, place upon it the scent of the rose so that it has the shape and the fragrance; then you see the artificial rose bright and not wilting. But the marvel is in the natural rose, that it wilts, because its wilting indicates that there is life in it.

Therefore God named man a creator (khaliq), and He was fair to him and honoured his bringing into existence of that which did not exist. Yet He, glorified be He, is the best of creators. The aspect of His excellence is that God created from nothing, while you created from something existing. God created a creation in which there is life, growth and reproduction; you created a thing that remains rigid in its original state. Nevertheless your Lord has been fair to you.

As for His saying, exalted be He: ﴿I create for you from clay like the form of a bird...﴾ (Al 'Imran): it is known that it is within the capacity of every person to shape a bird from clay and fashion it in its form. But is it said of him that he created a bird by this shaping? Is the marvel in shaping it in the form of a bird? The marvel is in breathing life into it, and this is only from God. Therefore 'Isa, peace be upon him, said: ﴿then I will breathe into it and it will be a bird by permission of God...﴾ (Al 'Imran).

If we grant that they create something, they are at the same time created. More astonishing than this is that the one they take as a god cannot even protect himself or set himself upright if the wind knocks him down; and if the god's arm is broken, they take him to repair him: the god in the hand of the worker to fix him! A strange thing, and foolish minds.

Therefore He, exalted be He, says of their gods: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides God will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it. And if the fly should steal from them a thing, they could not retrieve it from him. Weak are the seeker and the sought﴾ (al-Hajj).

Then He, glorified be He, says: ﴿and they control not for themselves any harm or benefit...﴾ (al-Furqan): meaning, they cannot benefit them if they are worshipped, nor harm them if they disbelieve in them. ﴿Nor do they control death or life or resurrection﴾ (al-Furqan): that is, death or life for others. They control none of this at all, because it is among the attributes of the true God who gives life and causes death, then raises people in the Hereafter. So, man has several stages: after having been non-existent, God brought him into existence; then death befalls him and he dies; then God resurrects him and gives him the life of the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 25, verse 4:

Then He, glorified is He, says:

﴿And those who disbelieve say, "This is nothing but a falsehood which he has invented, and other people have helped him at it. So they have certainly committed an injustice and a lie."﴾

After the Furqan (the Criterion) had spoken and distinguished in the matter of the Divine Essence (al-qimma), divinity, taking a son, and associates, and had separated the true God from the false god, He willed to speak of the Furqan in terms of the Message, relating what the disbelievers said about the Qur'an. ﴿"This is nothing but..."﴾ means: what is this, i.e. the Qur'an, which Muhammad recites? ﴿...a falsehood (ifk)﴾: al-ifk is the deliberate lie that inverts realities. We have already said that if a verbal attribution agrees with reality it is truth, and if it contradicts reality it is falsehood.

Ifk is an inversion of reality that makes what exists non-existent and what does not exist existent, as occurred in the incident of the slander (hadith al-ifk), when they accused 'A'isha, Mother of the Believers, of what contradicted reality. The reality was that Safwan (1) made his camel kneel for her so that she could mount it without him looking at her, and this indicates the utmost chastity and protection; yet in their slander they turned purity and chastity into immorality.

It is remarkable that those who accused the Qur'an of being a falsehood are the very same people who said of it:

﴿"Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of the two cities, a great one?"﴾ (az-Zukhruf 43:31). So they acknowledge the Qur'an and bear witness to it, but what troubles and vexes them is that it was sent down upon Muhammad specifically; had it been sent down, hypothetically, upon someone other than Muhammad, they would have believed in it.

And from their folly is their saying:

﴿"O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ (al-Anfal 8:32).

The logical course would have been to say, "Guide us to it," but it is stubbornness and arrogance.

His saying ﴿...which he has invented (iftarahu)﴾ means: he claimed it. How strange is the state of these people: they accuse the Qur'an of being a falsehood that was fabricated, so why do they not fabricate something like it themselves, when they are a people of eloquence and clear expression?

In another place He, exalted is He, says:

﴿"And We certainly know that they say, 'It is only a human who teaches him.' The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is clear Arabic speech."﴾ (an-Nahl 16:103).

Long ago they said: "If you are a liar, then be a male" (i.e., show your manhood by bringing forth a proof). Otherwise, how can you accuse Muhammad that a foreign man teaches him the Qur'an, when the Qur'an is in Arabic?

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿"...and other people helped him at it"﴾: the one who uttered this saying was an-Nadr ibn al-Harith, and after he said it, others repeated it after him, such as 'Addas, Yasar, and Abu Fukayha al-Rumi. The Qur'an refutes all these accusations.

﴿"...so they have certainly committed an injustice (zulm) and a lie (zur)"﴾: meaning they passed judgment on it. Zulm is passing judgment without right, and zur is the falsity of the judgment and its evidence. Zulm comes after zur, because the judge first hears the testimony and then bases the ruling upon it; if the testimony is false testimony, the ruling then becomes zulm.

But the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says ﴿"injustice and a lie"﴾, and this is evidence that the judgment came from them in advance, and then they sought an evidence for it.

(1) He is Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal ibn Rahda al-Sulami al-Dhakwani, Abu 'Amr: a Companion who witnessed the Battle of the Trench and all the campaigns, attended the conquest of Damascus, and was martyred in Armenia in the year 19 AH. (al-A'lam of al-Zirikli, 3/206).

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And they say, "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾

Al-Asatir (sing. ustura, "legend" or "fable"): the plural of ustura, like a'ajib, the plural of a'jouba (wonder), and ahadith, the plural of uhdutha (tale). Al-Bukra is the beginning of the day, and al-Asil is its end. The meaning is that they said about the Qur'an that it is stories and fables of the earlier peoples. ﴿Has had written down…﴾ (al-Furqan 25:5) means: he ordered them to be written. This is from their confusion and the inconsistency of their statements, for the Prophet (ﷺ) was unlettered; he could neither read nor write. Their saying ﴿and they are dictated to him morning and evening﴾ (al-Furqan 25:5) means: continually, so that he would repeat them and memorize them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 25, verse 6:

The Qur'an responds to them:

﴿Say: He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth has sent it down. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ 

﴿Sent it down...﴾ (al-Furqan): That is, the Qur'an was sent down once, all at once, from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the lowest heaven (al-sama' al-dunya).

﴿He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth...﴾ (al-Furqan): So do not think that by merely being created you have the power to uncover the secrets of God in His creation. Rather, until the Hour is established you will continue to stand before one secret and stand before another.

Why? Because the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wants to nullify these pretensions, and brings forth unseen matters that did not occur to the contemporaries of Muhammad, and these matters become clear over the course of the centuries, even though the Qur'an was revealed to an unlettered (ummi) nation, and the Messenger to whom the Qur'an was revealed was an unlettered man. Yet despite this, the Qur'an reveals to us each day a new sign of God's signs.

As He, glorified is He, said: ﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth...﴾ (Fussilat, 53).

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, disclosed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, some of the unseen matters, so that his contemporaries might see them, to silence the disbelievers who accused him of being a liar. He thus disclosed some secrets, as happened at Badr. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on the battlefield, pointing with his staff at the places where the disbelievers would fall, and saying, "This is the place where Abu Jahl will fall, and this is the place where Utba ibn Rabi'a will fall..." (1)... etc., marking out on the ground the places where the people would fall.

Who could judge in advance a battle in which there is attack and retreat, striking and movement, and then say: So-and-so will die in this place?

And al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, about whom the Qur'an said (2) ﴿We shall brand him on the snout﴾ (al-Qalam, 16): That is, a blow will strike his nose, leaving a mark that will stay with him. After the battle, the people looked for him and found him just so.

These are all secrets of the cosmos which the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, informs His Messenger of, and the Messenger informs his community of them in circumstances where there is no expectation of knowing them.

Among this is what is reported: that the two daughters of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were married to two sons of Abu Lahab. When enmity arose between him and the Messenger of God, he ordered his two sons to divorce the daughters of the Messenger of God. Afterwards, one of the two sons saw the Messenger of God walking, so he spat in his direction, and the Messenger of God saw that and said to him: "May a dog of God's dogs devour you" (3) (4). Abu Lahab, after learning of this supplication, said: I fear for my son from the supplication of Muhammad.

It is strange that these disbelievers fear the supplication of the Messenger of God, when he is the one they accuse of sorcery and lying and disbelieve in him and his call.

When this son went out on a trading journey to al-Sham, the people entrusted him to guard him and to place around him a barrier of their goods to protect him, fearing that the supplication of Muhammad might take effect on him. This is illogical from him, for he knows the truthfulness of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that he is sent from God; but his malice toward the Messenger of God and his arrogance toward the truth prevent him from faith.

The son set out on the trading journey, and despite their precautions in protecting him, a beast of prey attacked him one night and snatched him from among his companions. They were astonished, because the Messenger of God had said, "a dog of the dogs of God," and this was a lion, not a dog. The scholars said: Since the Messenger of God attributed the dog to God, the dog of God can only be a lion.

The meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, in response to them and to nullify their claims: ﴿He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth has sent it down...﴾ (al-Furqan). And He will expose you and nullify your fabrication against the Messenger of God, from your saying that it is a lie, falsehood, a fabrication, and the tales of the ancients; and He will humiliate you before the eyes of all the people.

In the time of the Messenger of God a battle took place between the Persians and the Byzantines, in which the Byzantines were defeated, so the Messenger of God was saddened by the defeat of the Byzantines, because they were People of the Book who believe in God and the messengers, whereas the Persians were disbelievers who did not believe in God and worshipped fire and other things. Although both agreed in denying the Messenger of God, the Byzantines' belief in God made the Messenger of God partisan toward them, even though they disbelieved in Him; for the partisanship of the Messenger of God belongs only to his Lord, mighty and majestic.

When the Messenger of God grieved over that, God, exalted is He, sent down to him: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Byzantines have been defeated in the nearest land, but after their defeat they will overcome within a few years. To God belongs the command, before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God...﴾ (al-Rum, 1-5).

What intellect could judge a battle that will occur several years from now? If the battle were to take place tomorrow, its outcome could be predicted based on calculating numbers, equipment, and military capabilities. But who can judge a battle whose wheels will turn after seven years? And who would dare to say it as a Qur'an that is recited and worshipped by until the Day of Resurrection? For if this period had passed and what the Messenger of God had foretold had not happened, those who believed would have disbelieved and those around him would have dispersed from him.

Therefore: the Messenger of God would not have said it as a Qur'an recited and worshipped by, except while certain of the truth of what he reported, because the One who informs him is his Lord, mighty and majestic, who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said here: ﴿Say: He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth has sent it down...﴾ (al-Furqan).

Strikingly, the Byzantines defeated the Persians on the same day that faith triumphed over disbelief at the Battle of Badr, the day of which God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God...﴾ (al-Rum).

And since He who sent down the Qur'an is He, glorified is He, who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth, there will never be any contradiction between the wording of the Qur'an and the wording of the cosmos, for their Creator is One, glorified and exalted is He. So whence would any discord or contradiction come?

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (al-Furqan). What is the connection of speaking of forgiveness and mercy here? They said: Because God, blessed and exalted is He, wants to leave open for these people who are being rebuked a space for repentance and a path back to Him, mighty and majestic, and to the domain of faith.

Therefore the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to someone who advised him to kill the disbelievers: "Perhaps God will bring forth from their loins someone who will worship God alone, associating nothing with Him" (5).

The Companions would suffer the greatest pain if any head of disbelief escaped being killed in battle, as happened with Khalid ibn al-Walid and Amr ibn al-'As before their Islam, while they did not know that God, exalted is He, was preserving them for Islam later on.

So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (al-Furqan): so that the path of return to faith in Muhammad is not cut off for one who was a disbeliever in him; so that He says to them: despite what has happened from you, if you return to the right path and to the enclosure of faith, then forgiveness and mercy from God await you.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, clarifies this matter for us even in the emotional impulses of creation: Hind bint 'Utba (6), who incited Wahshi (7)

to kill Hamza, the uncle of the Messenger of God, the lion of God and the lion of His Messenger, and she did not stop there, but mutilated him after his death, and chewed his liver, may God be pleased with him. Nevertheless, after she embraced Islam and pledged allegiance to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, she forgot this deed as though it had never happened.

When someone said to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: "This is the killer of your brother" (pointing to him), meaning Zayd ibn al-Khattab (9), 'Umar's only response was: "What should I do with him, when God has guided him to Islam?"

1 Related by Muslim in his Sahih (1779), and Ahmad in his Musnad (3/219-258), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, who said: "None of them moved from the place of the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace." Al-Nawawi said: "fa ma maat" means "did not move away."
2 Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (8/662): "There is disagreement about who the verse was revealed about. It is said to be al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and Yahya ibn Salam mentioned it in his tafsir. It is said to be al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth, mentioned by Sanad ibn Dawud in his tafsir. It is said to be al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, mentioned by al-Suhayli from al-Qutaybi. Al-Tabari related these two views."
3 Al-kalb: every ravening beast of prey, including the lion. Ibn Sayyid said: the term kalb became specific to the barking type of this species. It may also apply to the leopard and birds of prey (Lisan al-'Arab, root k-l-b). See also Fath al-Bari (4/39).
4 This is because 'Utayba ibn Abi Lahab, when he separated from Umm Kulthum, daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to the Prophet and said: "I have disbelieved in your religion and divorced your daughter; I will not love you and you will not love me." Then he attacked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and tore his shirt. The Messenger of God said: "As for me, I ask God to set His dog upon him." (6/19). He attributed it to al-Tabarani as a mursal report and said: "In its chain is Zuhayr ibn al-'Ala', who is weak." It was also related by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (2/539) from the hadith of Abu 'Aqrab, and he authenticated it; and Ibn Hajar graded it as hasan in al-Fath (4/39).
5 Al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3231, 7389), and similarly Muslim in his Sahih (1795), related from the hadith of 'A'isha, may God be pleased with her, that Jibril, peace be upon him, said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: "God has heard the words of your people to you and their reply to you. God has sent to them the angel of the mountains so that you may command him as you wish concerning them." The angel of the mountains called me, greeted me, and then said: "O Muhammad, if you wish, I will bring the two mountains down upon them." The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Rather, I hope that God will bring forth from their loins those who worship God alone, associating nothing with Him."
6 She is Hind bint 'Utba ibn Rabi'a al-Qurashiyya, mother of Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan. She witnessed Uhud on the side of the polytheists and did what she did to Hamza. She embraced Islam on the day of the Conquest, and died during the caliphate of 'Uthman. (al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba 8/206).
7 He is Wahshi ibn Harb al-Habashi, freedman of Banu Nawfal. He killed Hamza, the uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to keep his face hidden from him. He took part in the wars of apostasy (al-Ridda), in the killing of Musaylima, and witnessed the battle of al-Yarmuk. Then he settled in Homs and died there, and he lived until the caliphate of 'Uthman. (al-Isaba, biography no. 9110).
8 Lak: to chew. It is chewing a hard thing, turning it in your mouth. Al-luk: moving a thing around in the mouth. (Lisan al-'Arab, root l-w-k).
9 He is Zayd ibn al-Khattab ibn Nufayl al-'Adawi, paternal brother of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab; his mother was Asma' bint Wahb of Banu Asad, while 'Umar's mother was Hantama bint Hisham al-Makhzumiyya. Zayd was older than 'Umar, embraced Islam before him, witnessed Badr and the other battles, and was martyred at al-Yamama. (Tamyiz al-Sahaba 3/27).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 7:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) (subhanahu) says:

﴿And they say: "What is this messenger that he eats food and walks through the markets? Why was an angel not sent down to him, to be with him as a warner?"﴾

Wondrous is the matter of these obstinate opponents. They object to the Messenger of Allah eating food and walking through the markets in search of a livelihood. But have they ever seen a prophet who does not eat food or walk through the markets? Had the matter been so, their objection would have had some meaning. Therefore, their saying: ﴿What is this messenger that he eats food and walks through the markets...﴾ is a statement without any proof from reality, aimed at finding a pretext against the Messenger of Allah through this issue.

So what do they want?

They said: ﴿Why was an angel not sent down to him, to be with him as a warner?﴾ It is true that the angel does not eat, but the meaning of ﴿Why was an angel not sent down to him...﴾ is: to support him. In that case, it would not change the matter at all, and the words of Muhammad would remain exactly the same, unchanged. Therefore, the angel would add nothing new to the message. Accordingly, their statement is sophistry and argument with no meaning.

As for the word ﴿to be with him as a warner﴾: they did not say "as a bringer of good news," which indicates their obstinacy and stubborn contention, and that they would never believe; therefore, the warning would never leave them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 8:

﴿Or a treasure be thrown down to him, or he have a garden from which to eat.﴾ And the wrongdoers say: ﴿You follow nothing but a man under enchantment.﴾ :

You notice that they descend into their obstinacy and contentiousness. After they asked for an angel, they say ﴿Or a treasure be thrown down to him﴾ (al-Furqan): meaning, it is sent down to him so that he may live from it. ﴿Or he have a garden from which to eat﴾ (al-Furqan): meaning, an orchard. ﴿And the wrongdoers say: You follow nothing but a man under enchantment﴾ (al-Furqan).

The mashur (one under enchantment) is the one whose intellect has been taken by sorcery. The intellect is what chooses between alternatives and orders one's actions. The one who has lost his intellect cannot be logical in his conduct or in his speech. Muhammad (ﷺ) is not like that. You know his character and trustworthiness, you call him "the Truthful, the Trustworthy," and you acknowledge the soundness of his conduct and his wisdom. How, then, do you say he is mad?

Therefore, the Exalted says in response to them: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. And indeed, for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed, you are of a great moral character.﴾ (al-Qalam).

Good character (khuluq) sets a person's conduct right, making it beneficial rather than corrupt. So how could one of great character be mad? Therefore: Muhammad is not enchanted.

In another place they said: "a sorcerer." And even supposing he (ﷺ) were a sorcerer, why did he not enchant you as he enchanted the believers in him? It is the confusion of falsehood, its wandering and its disorder in confrontation.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿Look how they coin comparisons for you, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way.﴾

﴿Look...﴾ (25:9): This is an address meant to console the Messenger of God and reassure him.

﴿how they coin comparisons for you...﴾ (25:9): That is, they accused you of various accusations. They said, "He is a sorcerer." They said, "He is bewitched." They said, "He is a poet." They said, "He is a soothsayer."

﴿so they have gone astray and cannot find a way﴾ (25:9): Because they speak falsehood, nonsense and contradiction in their speech.

﴿so they have gone astray...﴾ (25:9): That is, from the comparison that would truly describe you, so that they might turn away from you those who believe in you, and cause those who have not believed to persist in their disbelief. Thus they did not hit upon even one correct comparison; they said, "He is a sorcerer," and they lied; they said, "He is bewitched," and they lied.

﴿and cannot find a way﴾ (25:9): That is, to that.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 10:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces.﴾

﴿Blessed..﴾ (al-Furqan): As we said, He is exalted and great in His goodness. This is because the discourse here also contains a gift, embodied in the good that Allah, may He be exalted, bestowed upon His Messenger ﷺ. His giving, glory be to Him, is constant and never ceases, such that no good stops at His giving; rather His giving continues as an unbroken good. So if He gives you today, you know that what He has in store for tomorrow is better than what He gave you yesterday.

1 Occasion of revelation of the verse: Ibn 'Abbas said: When the polytheists reproached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for his poverty, they said: "What is with this Messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ grieved, so Gabriel descended from his Lord to console him, and said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. The Lord of Might sends you His peace and says to you: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets...﴾ (al-Furqan)." Gabriel said: "Rejoice, O Muhammad, here is Ridwan, keeper of Paradise, who has come to you with the good pleasure of your Lord." Ridwan came, greeted him, and then said: "O Muhammad, the Lord of Might sends you His peace," and with him was a casket of light shining, and he said: "Your Lord says to you: these are the keys to the treasuries of this world, along with what is not diminished for you of what He has in the Hereafter, equal to the wing of a gnat." He said: "O Ridwan, I have no need of them. Poverty is more beloved to me, and that I be a patient, grateful servant." Adapted and abridged (from Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi al-Naysaburi, pp. 190-191), and (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4869).

Then the Truly Majestic says:

﴿Nay, they deny the Hour, and We have prepared a blaze for whoever denies the Hour.﴾

The context turns away from the previous speech and returns to the matter of their denial and their refusal to believe in Muhammad (ﷺ), because faith is not in their interest. Faith entails reckoning and recompense, while they wish to persist in their falsehood, continue in their idle talk, recklessness and sins. Therefore they deceive themselves and lie to their own souls so that they may remain in their present state.

For this reason you see that those who waste themselves in this world, from the materialists, the atheists and the philosophers, wish that the question of religion were a corrupt and false matter, so they deny it with all the strength they possess. Religion, in their view, is something unreasonable, because if they were to acknowledge it, their calamity would be great.

The meaning of ﴿We have prepared...﴾ (al-Furqan 25:11) is: We have made ready and readied for them a blaze, because their disbelief in the Hour is what drew punishment upon them. Had they believed in it, and in meeting God, and in the reckoning and recompense, they would have been guided, kept to the straight path, and been saved from this blaze.

As for sa'ir (al-sa'ir, "blaze"): it is the name of the kindled fire that consumes everything before it, just as we say: a mad dog (kalb masur), [translator's note omitted].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 12:

Then He, glory be to Him, says describing it (the Fire): ﴿When it sees them from a far place, they will hear its raging and its roaring.﴾

The Truth, blessed and exalted, wants to present the Fire to us as a vivid image. It sees its people from afar and rages at them; in its fury it wants to leap upon them before they reach it.

Al-taghayyuz (raging, seething): a painful feeling within the soul that makes a person feel constricted by what he finds. From this we hear the saying: "I cannot bear it (anā aṭiqu min janābī)," meaning: because of what is inside him of rage, his inner being cannot contain it. As long as rage exceeds the soul's capacity and endurance, a person must feel constriction, as if he is about to burst.

For this reason, the Most High says about the Fire in another place: ﴿It nearly bursts apart from fury.﴾ (al-Mulk). Tamayyaz (bursting apart) means: its parts nearly separate from one another.

But why does the Fire burst with rage? They (the scholars) said: because the whole universe glorifies God, praises Him and gives thanks to its Lord. Therefore it rejoices in what is in accordance with nature and loves it, and it hates the disobedient. Do you not see that all existence rejoiced at the birth of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace? Inanimate things, plants and animals rejoiced and received glad tidings, because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to restore to humanity its harmony with the created universe made for it, and to restore the balance.

Yet despite this, we see among rational humans, possessors of choice, those who disbelieve. Therefore the Fire rages against those who have deviated from the system of glorification and praise, and who have accepted for themselves a state lower than that of inanimate things, plants and animals. Concerning this they say: "The place was narrow for them because of their disbelief" (nabā bihim al-makān min kufrihim), meaning the places on earth reject them and are constricted by their presence upon them, just as the earth rejoices in the obedient one and gives him life, because he is in harmony with it. Place and occupant are both included in the system of glorification and obedience.

It is concerning this matter that Imam Ali, may God be pleased with him, draws our attention, saying: "When a believer dies, two places weep for him: a place in the heavens and a place on earth. As for the earth, it is the place of his prayer, for he has been deprived of his prayer. As for his place in the heavens, it is the ascent of his good deed."(1)

The Truth, blessed and exalted, shows us this image in His saying: ﴿On the Day We say to Hell, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Is there any more?"﴾ (Qaf). The Fire longs for its people like one who eats and is never satisfied: however many of the disobedient are cast into it, it says: ﴿Is there any more?﴾ (Qaf).

The meaning of ﴿zafīran﴾ (roaring): the exhaled breath. In another place the Most High says: ﴿When they are cast into it, they hear its roaring while it boils over﴾ (al-Mulk). So He mentions that it has a shahīq (inhaling sob) and a zafīr (exhaling roar), and it is in a narrow place.

1 Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir (4/142) and attributed to Ibn Abi Hatim that Ali said: "There is no servant except that he has a place of prayer on earth and an ascent of his deed from heaven, and the family of Pharaoh had no good deed on earth nor a deed that ascends to heaven." And from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: "There is no servant except that he has two doors in heaven: a door from which his provision descends, and a door through which his deed and his words ascend. When he dies, both of them lose him and weep for him." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma': "Narrated by Abu Ya'la, and in its chain is Musa ibn Ubayda al-Rabadhi, who is weak."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 13:

﴿And when they are cast into it, into a narrow place, bound together, they will cry out there for destruction.﴾

So God gathers upon them torments of every kind, until one of them says, merely upon seeing the punishment: ﴿Would that I were dust!﴾ (An-Naba' 40). Here he calls out for woe and destruction, saying: "Woe to me! Destruction to me!" meaning: "My ruin, come and be present! This is your time to rescue me from what I am in of punishment, for nothing will save me from the punishment except annihilation." Therefore they say: "More severe than death is one who seeks death," in accordance with the saying of the poet:

"Enough of a disease for you that you see death as a cure,
and enough of what fate offers that it be a mere wish."

You can imagine the horror of a punishment that makes its sufferer wish for death and call for it for himself.

1 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "Indeed Hell will constrict upon the disbeliever like the constriction of the spearhead upon the spear." Recorded by Ibn al-Mubarak in his Raqa'iq (299, Zawa'id al-Zuhd), and cited by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (6/4871).

2 Muqarrinin (bound together): restrained/shackled. Said by Abu Salih. It was also said: fettered, their hands tied to their necks with shackles. It was also said: they are bound with the devils, i.e., each one of them is bound to his devil. (These sayings are cited by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (6/4871).)

3 The verse is by al-Mutanabbi (Diwan 4/281), and it is mentioned by Shihab al-Din Mahmud al-Halabi in *Sina'at al-Tarassul* (p. 252) among the examples of good openings (husn al-ibtida'at).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 14:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Do not call out for one destruction today; call out for many destructions.﴾

The Truth, exalted is He, rebukes and reproaches them: "Woe to your failure and your ruin!" Calling out for one destruction will not benefit you; rather, call out for destruction upon destruction and destruction upon destruction, because this is a matter that will never end. The punishment will pass them from one torment to another, until they cry out: ﴿O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us.' He said: 'Indeed, you will remain.'﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf 43:77]. This is a renewed punishment: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment...﴾ [Surah al-Nisa' 4:56].

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, mentions the contrast, so that it is more painful to the people of evil and more enraging to them. After the punishment, He mentions the reward for good and the magnitude of the recompense for obedience. Such contrasts are numerous in the Book of God, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire.﴾ [Surah al-Infitar 82:13-14].

And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So let them laugh a little, and let them weep much, as recompense for what they used to earn.﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah 9:82].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 25, verse 15:

Here, after mentioning the Fire and what it contains of groaning (shahiq) and roaring (zafir), He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say: "Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity which the righteous have been promised? It shall be a reward for them and a final destination."﴾

﴿Say﴾ (al-Furqan 15): It is a command to the Messenger of God to say this. Those addressed are the ones who raised objections to his prophethood, peace and blessings be upon him, with flimsy objections from among his contemporaries. They were floundering in these matters, as one who does not know the reality of them would flounder; their only aim was to confront the Messenger of God regarding his call. Confronting any prophet regarding his call by his contemporaries is a natural matter, because the messengers only come when corruption has spread.

We have already said that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, placed in every soul a faculty that makes a person do something, and then another faculty comes within him to blame him for it. At that point there is immunity within the person's self, and they call it the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwamah). But this faculty may be obliterated within him, so that all his faculties cooperate in evil, such that the soul with all its faculties becomes one that commands evil (ammarah bi'l-su'), and it is ammarah in the intensive form (sigha al-mubalaghah), not amirah (one who commands). That is, it has taken this matter as its trade (hirfah).

It is like when you see a man working on a piece of wood, and you say to him: "najjar" (carpenter). If he has taken it as his trade, and does nothing but that, you say to him: "najjar"; and similarly: "khaʾit" and "khayyat" (tailor). So the meaning of ammarah is: it no longer has any work in restraining from evil; rather, it constantly strengthens the impulses of evil in the soul, and they take root in it until they become its trade.

So what then is the stance?

It is necessary that Allah, glorified is He, place in the souls of other people the faculty of goodness, to confront the owners of these souls that command evil, confronting them with counsel, guidance and exhortation, and turning them away from evil toward good. If the whole society becomes corrupt, there is no restraining soul and no restraining society, and then the heavens must intervene with a new messenger.

And among Allah's mercy to the world is that He guaranteed to the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that the self-reproaching soul would exist among it, and He guaranteed that its society would continue to enjoin good and forbid evil. Therefore there is no need for a messenger after the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him. So immunity exists in the nation of Islam; and had this immunity not existed in the self first, and in society second, the heavens would have intervened after the Messenger of God with a new messenger and a new miracle to restore creation to its right guidance.

There is no doubt that in society there is a group that profits from this corruption and lives in luxury under its shade. It is natural, then, that they defend it, and natural that they confront the call of the Messenger, which came to balance the scales of society, and that they stand in ambush for him, because it threatens this utilitarianism and ends their interest.

And if the earlier messengers were subjected to such persecution, the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was subjected to many times what they had suffered, because his persecution, peace and blessings be upon him, came commensurate with the enormity of his mission. The messengers before him came each to his own people specifically, in a specific time; but his message, peace and blessings be upon him, came to all mankind, encompassing all time and all place until the Hour arises. So his mission must necessarily be more difficult.

These notables who profit from corruption in society think that if the Messenger of God is dangled the wealth and comfort, he may renounce his call and leave them the field. Therefore the chiefs of Quraysh gathered around the Messenger of God, offering him wealth, status and authority, to divert him from the call and turn him away from it. These are the ones our teacher Shaykh Musa called "the dozen of evil," and they were twelve men, among them: Abu al-Bakhtari(1), Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, Umayya ibn Khalaf, al-As ibn Wa'il, Utba ibn Rabi'a, Munabbih ibn al-Hajjaj, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Shayba ibn Rabi'a, and Nubayh ibn al-Hajjaj(2).

These men went to our master, the Messenger of God, saying: "We are a delegation of your people to you. We have come to present an excuse, so that no one may blame us afterward. If you want wealth, we will gather wealth for you; if you want honour, we will make you our lord; if you want kingship, we will make you king over us."

There is a difference between wealth and honour: wealth is when a person is rich, but perhaps has no honour and no standing among people; and there are those who have honour and lordship but have no wealth.

We note that they climbed in their bargaining with the Messenger of God from wealth to honour and lordship, and then to kingship. So what was his stance? His stance, peace and blessings be upon him, was the stance that God had prepared for him, when Gabriel, peace be upon him, offered him that God would make the mountains of Mecca gold for him. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Rather, I would be satisfied one day and give thanks, and be hungry three days and humble myself"(4).

In another situation, Gabriel said to him: "Your Lord gives you the choice to be a prophet-king or a prophet-servant." He said: "Rather, a prophet-servant"(5).

The prophet is the possessor of the heavenly method, and the king is one who possesses control such that no one can stand against him, like Solomon, peace be upon him, to whom God gave a kingdom that should not belong to anyone after him. Yet this kingdom was not sought in itself, as is evidenced by the fact that Solomon, peace be upon him, despite the kingdom he was given, ate only al-khushkar, that is, coarse unrefined dark bread (al-radda), while his servants and clients ate fine, pure flour(6). Solomon did not desire kingship for its own sake, but to be strengthened by it in his call, so that no one would oppose him in it.

Therefore, when the Queen of Sheba sent him a gift to win him over and divert him from what he sought, he replied: ﴿So when he came to Solomon, he said: "Will you provide me with wealth? What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you; rather, you rejoice in your gift."﴾ (al-Naml 36),

so she came to him humbled, saying: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself, and I have submitted with Solomon to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ (al-Naml 44).

So: this matter of wealth was presented to the Messenger of God before the Meccan unbelievers proposed it. If he rejected it from one who owns it, how would he accept it from one who owns nothing? Therefore he said to them: "By God, I have no need of what you say. I am not seeking wealth, nor kingship, nor honour; I am only the Messenger of God, sent to you, and with me is a Book containing your way. My Lord has commanded me to be for you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. If you come to what I love, you will have secured the share of this world and the Hereafter; and if you reject my word, I will be patient until God judges between us, and He is the best of judges"(7).

So they resorted to the uncle of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, hoping he could win him over. When his uncle spoke to him, he said his famous saying: "By God, if they placed the sun in my right hand and the moon in my left, on condition that I abandon this matter, I would not abandon it until God makes it manifest or I perish in its cause"(8).

﴿Is that﴾ (al-Furqan 15): that is: what you are in now of punishment, is it better, or the Garden of Eternity which the righteous have been promised? Judge for yourselves in this matter, and we will accept your judgment. It is a provocation to the people of the Fire, in that Allah has combined for them the suffering of torment with the sight of the people of Paradise and what they enjoy of bliss. Even if the first alone were sufficient, yet they are in torment while the people of Paradise come to rebuke them: "Look at what you have missed of bliss!"

It also contains a rebuke to them: there is no basis for comparison between Paradise and Fire, for you, for example, do not say: "Is honey better, or vinegar?" because it is a matter known by immediate knowledge.

We have already spoken about the Bridge (al-Sirat), and why it is laid over the back of Hell, and that everyone passes over it; because Allah, blessed and exalted is He, wants to give you, from the sights of the Fire over which you pass upon the Bridge, another blessing that reminds you of deliverance from the Fire before you enjoy the bliss of Paradise.

Therefore Allah does not bestow favour upon us merely by entering Paradise, but also by deliverance from the Fire. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed succeeded...﴾ (Al ʿImran 185).

So the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, mentions the Fire to us, and that among its attributes are such-and-such; but in the Hereafter we shall see it with our own eyes, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾ (al-Takathur 7). That will be when you are upon the Bridge, so you will praise Allah for Islam, which has saved you from the Fire and admitted you into Paradise; each blessing is greater than the other.

In His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity..."﴾ (al-Furqan 15): the word khayr (better) in the language revolves around two meanings: khayr which is opposed by sharr (evil), and khayr which is opposed by a greater khayr. As in the noble hadith: "The strong believer is better and more beloved to God than the weak believer, and there is good in each"(9). Both have good in them, though the good is greater in the strong believer. Usually in this construction min (from) comes: "this is better than that."

As for the khayr that is opposed by sharr, like His saying: ﴿Those are the best of creation﴾ (al-Bayyinah 7).

The garden, as we use it in worldly usage, is a place full of trees and crops that shelter the one who walks within it, or that keep its owner from leaving it for outside, because in it is everything he needs for his life, so that he can dispense with anything else. Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, followed it with His saying: ﴿the Eternity...﴾ (al-Furqan 15).

So the garden you see in this world, however great it may be, is not the Garden of Eternity, because it must come to an end; its lifespan is that of its worldly life. It is as if He, glorified is He, says to every owner of a garden in the world: Do not be deceived by your garden, for it will pass away. And the greatest grief for the one who rejoices is to be certain of its disappearance, as the poet said: "The greatest grief for me in joy is when its possessor is certain of its departure."

Therefore God, exalted is He, reassures His believing servants that the Garden He has promised them is the Garden of Eternity and permanence, where its bliss does not perish and its joy is not troubled; its pleasures are lasting, neither cut off nor forbidden.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿which the righteous have been promised﴾ (al-Furqan 15): the promise here is from Allah, who possesses all the means of fulfilling it. A promise is good news of something good before it comes, so that you may prepare to be among its people; its counterpart is warning (indhar), which is a threat of evil before it comes, so that you may avoid it and shun the causes of falling into it.

The word muttaqi (righteous) originally refers to one who places between himself and evil a protection (wiqayah), as He, glorified is He, says: ﴿So guard yourselves against the Fire﴾ (al-Baqarah 24): that is, place between yourselves and it a protection.

It is remarkable that He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Fear Allah﴾ (al-Baqarah 194) and says: ﴿So guard yourselves against the Fire﴾ (al-Baqarah 24). The meaning is: place between yourselves and the coercive attributes of His majesty a protection, for you cannot bear the attributes of His subjugation; and the Fire is one of the hosts of God among the attributes of His majesty. So it is as if He, exalted is He, said: Guard yourselves against the hosts of the attributes of majesty of God.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It shall be a reward...﴾ (al-Furqan 15): that is, a reward for what they had sent forward. This meaning is clear in His saying: ﴿Eat and drink with pleasure for what you sent forward in the days past﴾ (al-Haqqah 24). This is the reason for the bliss they are in: they had often been exhausted, oppressed and tortured; and the reward for one who was tortured in our religion is that we make him happy now in the Hereafter.

﴿And a final destination﴾ (al-Furqan 15): that is, they will return to it. So do not look at what you are in now, but look at what you will inevitably come to; and reflect on your existence in this world, that it is temporary and uncertain, and your existence in the Hereafter, that it is everlasting and never ends. Therefore they say: "Beware of entering a place whose way out you do not know."

1 Abu al-Bakhtari: his name is al-As ibn Hisham ibn al-Harith, as stated by Ibn Ishaq. Ibn Hisham said: he is al-As ibn Hashim.(al-Sira al-Nabawiyya 1/264).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 16:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿For them therein is whatever they wish, abiding eternally. It is ever upon your Lord a promise, to be asked for.﴾

In the previous verse He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿the Garden of eternity...﴾ (al-Furqan 15). Here He says: ﴿abiding eternally...﴾ (al-Furqan 16). This is one of the places where the superficial readers see repetition in the speech of Allah, although the difference between the two is clear. The first "khuld" (eternity) is of the Garden, whereas the second is for its people, such that they do not leave it and it does not leave them.

As for His saying: ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish...﴾ (al-Furqan 16): it is as if the distinction of the Garden is that whoever enters it has whatever he wishes. On this matter there is a point that we must pay attention to. ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish...﴾ (al-Furqan 16): that is, if you enter the Garden, then therein you have whatever you wish. Therefore, you have therein a wish of bliss, and you wish only for what you know of limited bliss, whereas in the Garden there is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

This promise is not fulfilled for the believer except in the Garden. As for in this world, no one attains everything he wishes, even the prophets. Do you not see that Noah, peace be upon him, asked his Lord to save his son, and He said: ﴿Indeed, my son is of my family...﴾ (Hud 45), so he was not granted what he wished.

And Muhammad (ﷺ), despite all the efforts, was unable to guide his uncle Abu Talib, and this could only happen in this world. Therefore know that when Allah, exalted is He, withholds from you what you wish in this world, He is only storing it up for you, as He wills, in the Hereafter, although many think this is deprivation, and far is Allah, exalted is He, from depriving His servant.

In His saying: ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish...﴾ (al-Furqan 16) there are other gifts, but your Lord gives you according to your knowledge of bliss, and He places a control upon you ("kontrol"). You ask and your Lord gives, and He stores up for you what is better than what He has given you.

The wish in the Hereafter will be with other dispositions and faculties than the dispositions and faculties of the wishes of this world. In the Hereafter, they are pure, clear souls that desire only good, unlike what we see in this world of faculties that desire evil, because the faculties here are governed by a rule of compulsion in some things and choice in others. Compulsion is in things you cannot move away from, such as sickness and death, for example, whereas choice is in the other matters.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿It is ever upon your Lord a promise, to be asked for.﴾ (al-Furqan 16). The promise, as we have said, is the good news of something good before its time. Some scholars hold that "wa'dan" here means "haqq" (a due right). But does anyone have a right with Allah?

In another place He, exalted is He, calls it a recompense (jaza'). So is it a promise or a recompense? We say: when the Truth, glory be to Him, prescribed the promise, it became a recompense, because the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, does not go back on His promise, and nothing prevents its fulfilment.

As for the word ﴿mas'ula﴾ (al-Furqan 16): who is the asker here? They said: Allah, exalted is He, taught us to ask Him, and read His saying: ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers...﴾ (Al 'Imran 194). So we ourselves have asked for it.

Likewise the angels asked for it, as He says, glory be to Him, on the tongue of the angels: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them...﴾ (Ghafir 8).

So the Garden is asked for by its owners, and asked for by the angels who seek forgiveness for us.¹

¹ Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated, through Sa'id ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, regarding His saying ﴿It is ever upon your Lord a promise, to be asked for﴾ (al-Furqan 16), that he said: the angels ask this for them in their saying ﴿and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them...﴾ (Ghafir 8). Sa'id said: I heard Abu Hazim say: when the Day of Resurrection comes, the believers will say: "Our Lord, we have done what You commanded us, so fulfil for us what You promised us," and that is His saying ﴿a promise, to be asked for﴾ (al-Furqan 16). Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/241).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 17:

﴿And on the Day He will gather them, and what they worshipped besides Allah, and He will say: "Did you lead these My servants astray, or did they themselves stray from the path?"﴾

His saying: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them...﴾ (al-Furqan) : al-Hashr (the gathering): the gathering of all people, from the time of Adam, peace be upon him, until the Hour is established, in one place and for one purpose. If we now suffer from the crowding and complain of the narrowness of the earth for its inhabitants, while we are in one generation, then what of a station in which all creatures are gathered, from Adam until the establishment of the Hour?

And worship ('ibadah): that the worshipper obeys the commands of the one he worships. So one should look at everyone whose command we obey: Is it a command from his own self, or a command conveyed from one above him, a messenger or a god? If the command is from his own self, then you must consider: is it permissible, or does it contradict a textual ruling of the Shari'ah? If it is permissible, there is no harm in obeying it; but if it opposes the Shari'ah, then if you obey it, you are in effect worshipping him besides Allah.

Thus: when the one who commands you to prayer, zakat, or fasting commands you, then before you obey him, you have obeyed the One who entrusted him with this trust. Those who obey those who command them in things contrary to the method of Allah have worshipped them besides Allah and made them gods to be obeyed, as the Most High said concerning the devils: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you...﴾ (al-An'am, 121). Others worshipped the tyrant (taghut), or worshipped the sun, the moon, the stars, or idols and inanimate things.

It is known that worshipping these inanimate things is false and erroneous worship. Worship is obedience to a command, and do inanimate things have any command over anyone? Worship, if it is valid in this sense, is directed at those who possess a command or temporal authority, such as monks, or devils, or angels, or 'Isa, peace be upon him, since some claimed his divinity, or the "Mighty" etc. The inanimate things are included with these by way of generality.

Therefore the Most High says: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them, and what they worshipped besides Allah...﴾ (al-Furqan): meaning: He will gather the worshipper in error and the worshipped in error together in one place. Why? Because when the worshipper finds himself in punishment, he may expect his worshipped one to rescue him from the punishment; but behold, it precedes him into the Fire and cuts off from him every hope of salvation.

And the saying of the Truthful, Exalted: ﴿Did you lead these My servants astray, or did they themselves stray from the path?﴾ (al-Furqan):

The address here is directed to those among them who understand, and there is no objection to its being for all of them. We speak of the law we know, and the Truth, Blessed and Exalted, has explained to us that everything has a language. So why do we rule out that the address here is to the rational and the non-rational, based on His saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it exalts His praise, but you do not understand their glorification...﴾ (al-Isra', 44).

Sulayman, peace be upon him, who was among those who understood glorification, said, when he heard the ant warning her people: ﴿"My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me..."﴾ (al-Ahqaf, 15), and ﴿"O ants, enter your dwellings..."﴾ (al-Naml, 18). Sulayman, peace be upon him, smiled at what he heard from the ant and called it speech. In refutation of those who say that the glorification here by the ant is a glorification of state, not of speech:

This is a view contrary to the text of the Qur'an, which says: ﴿But you do not understand their glorification...﴾ (al-Isra', 44). The Truth, Exalted, has ruled that you do not comprehend this glorification. If you say: it is glorification by indication, then you have understood it; but He, Exalted, has ruled that you do not understand it, unless Allah makes you know Him and informs you of the languages of these creatures.

And why do we rule out this matter when modern science now establishes that every nation of existing beings has its own language? Do we not now converse among ourselves in an unspoken language, the language of signals by which sailors, for example, communicate?

So the Truth, Exalted, asks the worshipped: ﴿"Did you lead these My servants astray...?"﴾ (al-Furqan, 17). And Allah knows whether they led them astray or not. Therefore 'Isa, peace be upon him, answered a question like this in His saying: ﴿And when Allah says, "O 'Isa, son of Maryam, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'" He said, "Exalted are You! It is not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself..."﴾ (al-Ma'idah, 116).

The question of Allah to the worshipped is a rebuke to the worshippers in front of those they worshipped; and had their worship been in truth, the worshipped would have defended them before Allah. Therefore 'Isa, peace be upon him, answered: ﴿"I did not say to them except what You commanded me: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.'"﴾ (al-Ma'idah, 117).

As for the others, they said: "We did not lead them astray; rather, they themselves strayed from the path."

And the word ﴿"My servants..."﴾ (al-Furqan, 17): it has already been said that 'abd is pluralized as 'ibad and 'abid, and 'abd means that he is subject to the command of the master and has no disposal from himself. If you look at it this way, then all of Allah's creation are 'abid, because there are things in which they do not go beyond the will of Allah, such as his birth in a particular form, his sickness, or his death.

Therefore we say to those who are accustomed to opposing the commands of Allah and rebelling against Him, Exalted: you may rebel against belief in Him and so disbelieve, you may rebel against belief in His Messenger and so deny, and you may rebel against a ruling of the rulings and oppose it.

So: you have boldness in opposition and familiarity with rebellion. And since you have practice in this, then you must also rebel at sickness and say: "I will not fall ill," and rebel against death and say: "I will not die." But far-fetched! These are matters in which all are slaves of Allah, subdued to His will, Exalted: the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient.

There are other matters which Allah has made subject to choice. Those for whom the Best Reward has preceded from Allah, and who have been inspired with success, surrender their choice for the choice of their Lord and His will, so they become slaves of Allah in all matters, both the compulsory and the non-compulsory. These are the ones who deserve to be called 'ibad of Allah.

So the 'ibad share with the 'abid in the compulsory matters, and are distinguished from them by surrendering their own will to the will of their Lord, and their choice to His choice, Mighty and Majestic. Therefore He named them 'ibad, as came in His saying, Exalted:

﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ (al-Furqan, 63).

The interrogative in His saying, Exalted: ﴿"Did you lead these My servants astray?"﴾ (al-Furqan, 17): some who are not qualified to understand from Allah say: "Would He not have said, 'Did you lead My servants astray?'" We say to them: you do not have the linguistic faculty to understand the Qur'an. You ask about the act when it is not present before you; you say: "Did you build the house that you told me you would build?" and he tells you: "I built it" or "I did not build it." But when you say: "Did you build this house?" the question is not about the building, but about its doer: are you or someone else? Because the building stands before you.

So: there is a difference between asking about the event and asking about the doer of the event. Here the error is present in fact, so the question is about the doer: ﴿"Did you lead these My servants astray, or did they themselves stray from the path?"﴾ (al-Furqan, 17).

He named them 'ibad here although they are astray, because the discussion concerns the Hereafter, where no one has choice any longer. Choice was in this world, and by it we distinguish between 'abid and 'ibad. But in the Hereafter all are 'abid and all are 'ibad, for what distinguished them has ceased, since they are all subdued and no one among them has choice.

Footnote 1: awza'ahu an yaf'ala kadha: pushed him, urged him and incited him, or inspired him and guided him. Allah says: ﴿"My Lord, enable me to be grateful..."﴾ (al-Ahqaf, 15), i.e., inspire me to Your gratitude, push me toward it and make it beloved to me. (al-Qamus al-Qawim, 2/334).

Footnote 2: walking with hawn: with tranquillity and dignity, as said by 'Ikrimah and Mujahid, as transmitted by Ibn Manzur in Lisan al-'Arab, entry: h-w-n.

"Glory be to You, it was not for us to take any protectors besides You, but You gave them and their fathers enjoyment until they forgot the Reminder, and they were a people doomed to ruin." (25:18)

Subhanaka (Glory be to You): glorifying God, exalting Him above resemblance in His essence, and exalting Him above resemblance in His attributes and actions. God has hearing and you have hearing, God has existence and you have existence, God has life and you have life. But is your life like the life of God?
