This too is one of the matters by which they reason themselves away from belief. How can they ask that the Qur'an be sent down all at once, when they cannot bear even one verse of it? Rather, it is mere disputation, sophistry and bankruptcy of argument, so their objection is to the Qur'an being sent down piecemeal (munajjaman)(1).

So, there is no fault in the Qur'an in their eyes; its defect, in their view, is that it was sent down to Muhammad specifically, and that it descends piecemeal rather than all at once, as if the capacity for faith among them were fitted to the Qur'an being sent down all at once!!

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Thus...﴾ (al-Furqan 32): meaning, We sent it down in this way, piecemeal, according to circumstances, and the wisdom in that is ﴿that We may strengthen your heart thereby...﴾ (al-Furqan 32): because you would encounter, over the course of twenty-three years, situations that shake one to the core. So whenever you encountered one of these situations, a portion of the Qur'an descended as consolation for you, as strengthening, and as a connection with the heavens that is never severed. Had the Qur'an been sent down once, the strengthening would have been once, and then the remaining events would come without strengthening. There is no doubt that the connection with the heavens strengthens the method and strengthens faith.

Moreover, if the Qur'an had been sent down once, how could they have asked about what they asked about, which the Qur'an recounts: "They ask you about such-and-such, they ask you about such-and-such..." etc. So its descent piecemeal is required by the wisdom of the Truthful One, glory be to Him, so that He may enumerate the situations of your strengthening, in accordance with the multiplicity of situations of harm done to you.

As for the meaning of ﴿and We have spaced it out in gradual recitation﴾ (al-Furqan 32): that is, We sent it down piecemeal according to circumstances, so that whenever a portion descended, you were able to memorize it and repeat it in prayer.

(1) Munajjaman: that is, divided and broken up according to events and the occasions of revelation, verse by verse. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/318): "al-Nasa'i narrated with his chain from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Qur'an was sent down all at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of Power, then it descended after that over twenty years."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 33:

﴿And they bring you no parable but We bring you the truth and the best explanation.﴾

The "parable" (mathal) is like their saying: ﴿Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?﴾ (al-Furqan 25:32), or their saying: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man of the two cities?﴾ (al-Zukhruf 43:31). The "parable" here means the strange things they demanded.

Had God answered them, they would have denied their own words and disowned them, as God said about the Jews: ﴿The foolish among the people will say: "What has turned them away from their qiblah which they used to face?"﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:142). Yet they still said what the Qur'an related of them. Was there not among them a man who would take heed of the Qur'an's words and warn them against this saying, so as to put the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in embarrassment, and show the Qur'an to be a lie, and say something contrary to reality? And then they could say: "The Qur'an said such-and-such, but this never happened from us"?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 25, verse 34:

﴿Those who will be gathered upon their faces to Hell — those are worse in position and further astray from the way.﴿34﴾﴾:

﴿Those who...﴾ (al-Furqan): a general reference to specific individuals known by their persons, who took a stance of hostility toward the Messenger. Among them are those who had earlier said: ﴿Oh, I wish I had taken a way with the Messenger! Woe to me! Oh, I wish I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend.﴾ And al-hashr (the gathering) means the assembling for reckoning, but they will be gathered upon their faces. Therefore, when this verse was revealed, they asked the Messenger of Allah: how will they walk upon their faces? The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He who made them walk upon their feet is able to make them walk upon their faces."(1)

So one who walks upon his face is like one who walks upon his belly, and perhaps he is dragged, whether upon his face or upon anything else. Moreover, a human being should not ask about matters that are the domain of absolute power.

And the Truth, blessed and exalted, clarifies this matter in His saying: ﴿And Allah created every moving creature from water. Of them are some that move on their bellies, and of them are some that walk on two legs, and of them are some that walk on four. Allah creates what He wills; indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ (al-Nur)

So walking is not confined to the modes we know; rather, it is the absoluteness of power that does what it wills.

But why did the Qur'an not mention the names of these wrongdoing persons who opposed Islam? They said: this is from the method of letting the opponent loose on the rein (irkha' al-'anan lil-khasm). The word "al-'anan" comes with the ʿayn vowelled with kasra and with fatha, and the lexicographers say: it is of the form of what it means. If you intend by it the "canopy of the sky" (ʿanan al-sama'), it is on the pattern of saḥāb (cloud); and if you intend by it the "rein of the horse" (ʿanan al-faras), it is on the pattern of lijam (bridle).

When the rider loosens the rein for his mount, he leaves it to walk as it wishes. Likewise, the Truth, blessed and exalted, loosens the rein for the opponent so that he says all that he has, and so that He may bring him to His side — not by what he dislikes, but by what he loves. Allah, exalted, taught His Messenger (ﷺ) how to respond to them and to argue with them with gentle argument, "with that which is better." So when they called him a fabricator (muftar), and the Qur'an fabricated and false, he responded to them: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "Then bring a surah like it..."﴾ (Yunus, 38).

Then he ascends in his argument with them: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime, and I am innocent of what you commit."﴾ (Hud, 35). And in another verse he answers them: ﴿And indeed, either we or you are upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ (Saba, 24)

Does the Prophet (ﷺ) not know who is upon guidance and who is upon error? There is no doubt that this is letting the opponent loose on the rein. He says to them: "I and you are at two opposite ends: I say there is one God, and you deny my word. So I contradict you in this matter, and the matter must come in one form: either I am upon guidance, or you are." And he does not claim the truth for himself.

Therefore, what is required is that you use your minds to distinguish which of us is upon guidance and which of us is upon error — as if the Messenger of Allah were content with their judgment in this matter. The Messenger of Allah did not leave them the judgment except while he was confident that, if they were free of desire, they would know that the truth was with him, that he was upon guidance, and that they were upon error.

Therefore, when the Qur'an spoke of the Quraysh disbelievers, who were obstinate in their proposals, were stubborn, and harmed the Messenger of Allah with every kind of harm, yet when it spoke of them it came in a general style and said: "Those who" (alladhina), and did not say "these," but brought the general matter and did not confront them with the recompense — which indicates gentleness in the matter of the call. This is a kind of winning over the opponent so that we cut off from him the ferocity of enmity and obstinacy.

Thus the Truth, blessed and exalted, addresses His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were lenient with them...﴾ (Al 'Imran, 159): as if you were not gentle with them by your nature, because their obstinacy and harm would have compelled your nature to be harsh with them; but the mercy of Allah encompassed you, so you were gentle with them. ﴿And if you had been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have dispersed from around you...﴾ (Al 'Imran, 159).

This means that the caller (da'iyah) must have a broad breast and a spacious domain, because he draws the people of error out of what they are accustomed to toward something they dislike; so do not draw them out by a method they dislike, lest you gather two hardships upon them. Rather, be gentle with them, as the Mighty and Majestic said to Musa and Harun when He commanded them to call Pharaoh: ﴿Speak to him gently; perhaps he will be reminded or fear.﴾ (Ta-Ha, 44)

Because one whose obstinacy has reached the point of arrogance not toward creatures like himself, but toward the Creator, claiming divinity — you must come to him with gentle, kind speech.

In another verse, the Truth, glorified, teaches His Messenger (ﷺ) how to argue with the polytheists. He, glorified, says: ﴿Say, "You will not be asked about what we committed, and we will not be asked about what you do."﴾ (Saba, 25)

Can one imagine that crime would come from the Messenger of Allah? And in contrast: ﴿nor will we be asked about what you do﴾ (Saba, 25): although the logic of the argument here would be to say, "nor will we be asked about what you commit (tujrimun)," yet he attributed the crime to himself and did not mention it in regard to the others. Is there any gentleness and softening of hearts beyond this?

The Truth, blessed and exalted, sets out all these matters to establish that His Messenger (ﷺ) was eager for the faith of his people, and that he spared no effort in guiding them and drawing them to himself — to the extent that he burdened himself beyond what Allah required of him, until his Lord said to him: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them, if they do not believe in this message.﴾ (al-Kahf, 6)

And He said: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself, that they will not be believers.﴾ (al-Shu'ara', 3)

That is: destroying yourself for their guidance, while your duty is only to deliver the message. A Lord would not say this to His Messenger unless He knew from him zeal and a definite desire for the guidance of his people.

As for the meaning of ﴿They are worse in position and further astray from the way﴾ (al-Furqan, 34): He said "worse" (sharr) and did not say "worst" (asharr), because its meaning is that the second party has evil in it; and this too is from letting the opponent loose on the rein.

(1) On the authority of Anas ibn Malik that a man said: "O Prophet of Allah, will the disbeliever be gathered upon his face on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Is not He who made him walk on his two feet in the world able to make him walk upon his face on the Day of Resurrection?" Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4760-6523) and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2806), Book of the Attributes of the Hypocrites.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, tells us about the peoples of the earlier messengers:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, and We made his brother Aaron with him a minister.﴾ (35)

The saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, has already preceded: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals...﴾ (31) (al-Furqan). So every prophet must have enemies, because he came to rebalance the scale of noble conduct, which was governed by arrogant, tyrannical people, and by corrupters who would be deprived of the fruit of this corruption; it is natural that they would stand in the way of the call.

For this reason, the Truth, glorified is He, sets forth for His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, some examples from the procession of the messages, saying: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, and We made his brother Aaron with him a minister.﴾ (al-Furqan, 35).

It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, were saying to His Messenger: You have encountered the hardship of calling people who do not believe in God. As for Moses, he encountered the call of one who claimed to be a god. So there are those who bore many hardships in the way of the call, to the degree that Moses, peace be upon him, saw that he would not be able to carry out this task alone.

So we see him, though he is the prophet and messenger whom God chose, saying: ﴿And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent in tongue than I, so send him with me as a helper to confirm me...﴾ (34) (al-Qasas). This means that Moses, peace be upon him, knew the extent of the hardship and the magnitude of the task he would undertake.

The earlier messages were sent by the messenger to his own nation, limited in time and in place, and despite that they encountered hardships. As for you, O Muhammad, you were sent with a message general in time and in place until the Hour is established, so your troubles must be like the troubles of all those who preceded you.

Note on the footnote: **al-Wazir** (minister, helper, assistant). Al-Sha'rawi quotes Lisan al-Arab (root: w-z-r): "The word wazir in language is derived from al-wizr (burden/weight), and al-wazir is the rope by which one holds fast to be saved from destruction; likewise the wazir of the caliph means the one who relies on his opinion in his affairs and whom he resorts to."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 36:

﴿Then We said, "Go to the people who denied Our signs." So We destroyed them with complete destruction.﴾

The address in ﴿Go...﴾ (al-Furqan) is to the Messenger Musa (Moses), and to his minister Harun (Aaron). He said: ﴿to the people who denied Our signs...﴾ (al-Furqan), even though among them was one who claimed divinity, as a continuation of giving rein to the opponent, for Pharaoh denied that it is among the signs of God that one should believe in one God.

Then the outcome was ﴿So We destroyed them with complete destruction﴾ (al-Furqan), because they stood against Musa and Harun in a stance of hostility, and a battle took place between them in which the Exalted God intervened, and He destroyed them with complete destruction, as if the Exalted God were saying to His Messenger: Be at ease, for if they deviate from the path of truth and refuse to come to you willingly, their end will be like the end of those.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 25, verse 37:

﴿And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them, and made them a sign for mankind; and We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.﴾

The Truthful One, blessed and exalted is He, mentioned Noah after Moses, peace be upon them both, because each of them was distinguished in his call by something, and each of them bore various kinds of hardship. Moses confronted one who claimed divinity, while Noah held a vast temporal authority that encompassed everyone existing on the earth in his time. This does not mean that he, peace be upon him, was sent to all people; rather, his people were the ones existing on the earth at that time, for he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years.

Read his story, peace be upon him, in Surah Nuh, so that you may see the extent of his suffering in calling his people throughout this period, and yet only a few believed with him, and the victory was his in the end.

Also, because he, peace be upon him, was exposed to a matter related to sonship: sonship in the method, and sonship in lineage. His son, by lineage, was a disbeliever, and he could not guide him. When he said to his Lord, mighty and majestic is He, ﴿Indeed, my son is of my family...﴾ (Hud 45), He said to him: ﴿O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous...﴾ (Hud 46).

So He made the ground of negation ﴿indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous﴾ (Hud 46). Thus lineage here is deeds and obedience. It is as if the prophethood of the prophets is sonship of deed, not sonship of lineage: your true son is the one who walks in your method, even if he is not of your blood.

Another matter we notice in the pairing of Moses and Noah, peace be upon them, in the context of consoling the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), is that they share a cosmic phenomenon worthy of reflection and contemplation. For every manifestation of the cosmos before us, if we investigate each of its manifestations with reason, deliberation and certainty, we could derive from it what enriches our lives, makes them luxurious and makes them happy.

Therefore the Truthful One, blessed and exalted is He, reproaches those who turn away from contemplating His signs, saying: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it?﴾ (Yusuf 105).

We have already said: all the inventions that made people's lives comfortable and happy, reduced their efforts, and shortened time for them, were the result of observation and reflection on the manifestations of the cosmos, like the one who invented the wheel, the steam engine... etc.

Here we notice that the relation between Moses and Noah, peace be upon them, is that God, exalted is He, destroys and saves with one and the same thing. The water that saved Moses is the water that drowned Pharaoh, and the water that saved Noah is the water that drowned the disbelievers of his people. This is a consolation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): if God wills deliverance, He delivers; if He wills destruction, He destroys, even with one and the same thing.

Do you not see that the companions of Moses, when they saw the sea before them and Pharaoh behind them, said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken!﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 61). This is a reality and a cosmic fact: who can reverse it? Only Moses reversed it, saying "Kalla" (no!), we shall not be overtaken. He said it with full force, not by his humanity, but by the lordship in which he trusted that it would not hand him over: ﴿He said, "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 62).

And so was the matter of Noah, peace be upon him, but in another way: the ship. The idea of the ship did not exist before Noah, peace be upon him. Did it not occur to someone that a tree thrown into water floats on its surface, and he reflected on the apparent buoyancy, and how the tree did not sink into the water? Skilled carpenters used to measure the density of wood by throwing it into water, then looking at how much of it was submerged, and by this they knew its density.

This phenomenon, to which Archimedes drew attention and on which he built the theory of floating bodies and displaced water, and through which he reached the principles: by it things float or sink in water. If density increases, the object becomes heavy and sinks in water; if density decreases, it floats.

You observe this if you throw a coin, for example, and it floats, although the mass is the same. Yes, the mass is the same, but the displaced water in the second case is greater, so it helps it float.

The Truthful One, blessed and exalted is He, wanted to draw man's attention to these phenomena and guide him to the making of ships that carry him on the water, because three quarters of the earth's surface is water. God has provided you with means of transport on the quarter; will He not provide you with transport on the three quarters, so that you may take the bounties of the sea as you have taken the bounties of the land?

Consider the style of the Qur'an: ﴿And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers...﴾ (al-Furqan 37). It is known that they denied their messenger Noah, not all the messengers. They said: because prophethood does not bring contradictory things; it brings matters agreed upon. Therefore He made the denial of one messenger like the denial of all the messengers.

Then He mentioned its consequence: ﴿We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind...﴾ (al-Furqan 37). The phrase ﴿We drowned them...﴾ (al-Furqan 37) means: the One who drowned the deniers saved the believers. The drowning of the deniers was the first act that answered their mockery of Noah, when they passed by him while he was building the ship: ﴿And whenever a company of his people passed by him, they mocked him. He said, "If you mock us, then we mock you as you mock."﴾ (Hud 38).

The drowning was not the end of the requital; rather it was its beginning, for there is the punishment awaiting them in the Hereafter: ﴿And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment﴾ (al-Furqan 37). Thus Allah combined for them drowning in this world and burning in the Hereafter.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, strikes for His Messenger another example:

﴿And 'Ad and Thamud and the People of the Rass, and generations between them, many.﴾ (25:38)

These are examples of the hardships that the Messengers faced from their peoples, as He said elsewhere: ﴿And to 'Ad, their brother Hud...﴾ (7:65). ﴿And to Thamud, their brother Salih...﴾ (7:73).

The outcome was that God gave victory to His allies and His Messengers, and repelled their adversaries and those who denied them. All of this is to tell His Messenger (ﷺ): "O Muhammad, you are not an innovation among the Messengers. If your people take a stance of obstinacy and denial, then be certain and confident of God's victory for you, as He said:

﴿And certainly Our word has preceded for Our servants, the Messengers. Indeed, they will be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers will be the predominant.﴾ (37:171–173)

This is a matter that the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, states not merely for recounting history, but for the training of the human soul. If you desire victory, then be among the soldiers of God and under His party, and you will never be defeated—except if this soldiership becomes corrupted in you. Do not forget that the first thing in this soldiership is obedience and discipline. So if you are defeated in a battle, then you must examine from which of these two you withdrew.

Therefore, we see at the Battle of Uhud that the disobedience of the archers to the command of the Messenger of God, the commander of the battle, was the cause of the defeat (1). And what if they had been victorious despite their disobedience of the Messenger's command? Had they been victorious, they would have understood that obedience and compliance with the command of the Messenger of God are not necessary. So this is evidence for the obligation of obedience, and that they should never step outside the soldiership of faith, in submission and obedience. And do not say: "The Messenger is among us, so he will train you," for he will not remain among you forever.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the People of the Rass...﴾ (25:38): ar-Rass is the well or the pit. It was in al-Yamama, and they called it al-Ukhdud (the trench), and its mention occurs in Surat al-Buruj.

Here He, glorified is He, has said: ﴿and generations between them, many﴾ (25:38). The Truth, glorified is He, did not intend to enumerate all the previous nations; He sufficed with mentioning examples of them. In other places He gathers them together collectively, saying, exalted is He: ﴿So each We seized for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of pebbles (2), and among them were those seized by the blast, and among them those We caused the earth to swallow, and among them those We drowned...﴾ (29:40).

1 The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed over the archers 'Abd Allah ibn Jubayr, and the archers were fifty men. He said to him, may God bless him and grant him peace: "Repel the cavalry from us with arrows; let them not come at us from behind. Whether we have the upper hand or they do, hold your position; we shall not be attacked from your side." (Dala'il al-Nubuwwa 3/227). In another narration (3/229): the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: "If you see us being snatched by birds, do not leave this place until I send for you, and if you see us having defeated the people and trampled them, do not leave until I send for you." Then the spoils appeared to them, and the archers said: "The spoils! Your companions have prevailed, so what are you waiting for?" 'Abd Allah ibn Jubayr said: "Have you forgotten what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to you?" They said: "We will certainly go to the people and take a share of the spoils." So they went to them, their faces were turned, and they were routed.

2 Hasaba: to pelt him with pebbles. Al-Hasib: a violent whirlwind that pelts you with pebbles and destroys you; and violent winds do even more than that. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/156).

And to each We set forth parables, and to each We brought utter destruction. (Surah al-Furqan 25:39)

Commentary:

"And to each" (﴿وكلا﴾): i.e., each of those mentioned earlier.

"We set forth parables" (﴿ضربنا له الأمثال﴾): meaning: I did not leave any messenger without bringing him a lesson from a messenger before him. I would say to him: "Look at those who came before you: how their people denied them, how they opposed them and took this stance against them, and yet victory over them was his." This is so that every prophet may take a store of steadfastness and strength by which he stands firm before the hardships of the call, so that he does not weaken or despair, and so that he may be certain that the final outcome is his and in his favour.

"And to each We brought utter destruction" (﴿وكلا تبرنا تتبيرا﴾): i.e., We destroyed and annihilated everyone who denied the messengers, with various and diverse kinds of punishment. Some of them were punished with the Blast (al-sayha), or by being swallowed up by the earth (al-khasf), or by drowning (al-ighraq), or by the furious violent wind (al-rih al-sarsar al-'atiya).

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 25, verse 40:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And they have certainly passed by the town upon which was rained a rain of evil. Have they not been seeing it? Rather, they did not expect resurrection.﴾

These scenes were not merely history that the Qur'an recounts. They are scenes and sights that the Meccan disbelievers saw during the summer journey, when they passed by these dwellings, as He, glorified is He, said in another place: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not then reason?﴾ (al-Saffat). So this history has a reality that supports it and traces that indicate it.

The town upon which was rained a rain of evil is Sodom, the town of the people of Lot. ﴿Have they not been seeing it...﴾ (al-Furqan): did they not witness it in their journeys?

﴿Rather, they did not expect resurrection﴾ (al-Furqan): The word "bal" (rather) is for idrab (a turning away from what precedes), so it negates what comes before it and affirms what follows. The meaning is: they passed by it and witnessed it, and they know it perfectly well, but they do not expect resurrection, meaning: they do not await the raising (ba'th), do not believe in it, and do not acknowledge standing before God for reckoning. Did they not say: ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?﴾ (al-Mu'minun).

It is strange that these people do not believe in resurrection and reckoning, when they themselves, whenever they saw an oppressor, would stand against him and prevent him from oppressing, as in the Pact of al-Fudul (hilf al-fudul), for example. They would seize the oppressor and punish him until he returned from his oppression, then return to the oppressed his right. But did they not consider the state of the oppressors who passed through this world without punishment and without retribution? Is it not just that there should be another abode in which they are called to account?

For this reason, we used to respond to the Communists with this matter. We would say to them: You tortured your enemies from among the feudal lords and the capitalists and took revenge on them, so what about those who preceded you and whom you did not reach? Is it not just that you acknowledge a comprehensive Day in which these people will be held to account?

When a speaker said: "A wrongdoer will not die until God takes vengeance on him," they said to him: "So-and-so, the oppressor, has died, and we did not see anything in him." He said: "Behind this abode there is an abode in which the good-doer is recompensed for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil."

Footnote 1: The intended people are the Quraysh polytheists, for they used to pass by the town of the people of Lot in the summer during their journey to the Levant (al-Sham) in summer.

When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, had presented some examples from the procession of the prophets to console His Messenger (ﷺ), He makes clear that the matter with these disbelievers will not stop at obstinacy and insisting on frivolous demands. Rather, it goes further, to an attempt to mock him and ridicule him. So He, glorified is He, says:

﴿And when they see you, they take you only as a mockery: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"﴾ [25:41]

"In" here is a negation, meaning: "They take you only as a mockery." Then He mentions the form of the mockery: ﴿Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?﴾ (al-Furqan). In another place they said: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods...?﴾ (al-Anbiya' 21:36). It is as if he (ﷺ) is of a lower rank in their view. And since the Messenger, in their view, is of a lower rank than this, they want a person of the rank [they consider fitting], as they said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two towns?﴾ (al-Zukhruf 43:31).

The meaning of this is that they believe in the necessity of the existence of a God, a messenger and a method; their whole objection is that the message should be in Muhammad specifically.

Then they contradict themselves, saying:

﴿Indeed, he almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in adhering to them. But they will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in the way.﴾

How then do you mock him, and regard him as beneath the level of prophethood, and yet say that he almost led you astray from your gods? That is, he came close to leading you astray from your gods, despite your obstinacy and stubbornness. This is evidence and testimony for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he was strong, that he was on the level of prophethood, and that he spared no effort in calling you, to the point that he almost turned you away from your gods.

The proof that they were afraid of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) influence upon them is their saying to their followers when they saw them listening to the Qur'an: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during its recitation, so that you may prevail﴾ (Fussilat 41:26). So they wish to create confusion around the Qur'an, because they know its effect on souls, and they are a people of eloquence and rhetoric. If they hear the Qur'an, it must affect their hearts and draw them to it.

Do you not see the story of the conversion of Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), and how he was before Islam, harsh and tyrannical? When the opportunity presented itself and he listened to the Qur'an, he found in it a sound disposition and a pure natural inclination. The incident of his striking his sister and wounding her brought him back to the soundness of his nature and inner disposition. So when he heard the Qur'an from her and found in it a pure heart and a sound nature, he was affected by it, and he hastened to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to declare his Islam.

So then, your saying ﴿Indeed, he almost led us astray from our gods...﴾ (al-Furqan 25:42) is evidence that he is fit for the task for which he was sent. This contradicts your mocking and derisive saying ﴿Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?﴾ (al-Furqan 25:41).

As for their saying ﴿had we not been steadfast in adhering to them...﴾ (al-Furqan 25:42): it indicates that the Prophet (ﷺ) did things with them that required them to be steadfast (1) in error. ﴿But they will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in the way﴾ (al-Furqan 25:42): they will come to know this, but after it is too late, and when this knowledge no longer benefits them.

(1) Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/4911): "That is, we restrained ourselves upon worshipping them."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 25, verse 43:

﴿Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god? Would you then be responsible for him?﴾

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, lays down for His Messenger (ﷺ) a principle: that religion came only to protect people from the desires of people. Every human soul has a desire, and every person is pleased with his own desire. And since this is so, he will not submit to anyone else, because the other also has a desire. Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted...﴾ (al-Mu'minun 23:71).

But why do desires differ? They said: because the nature of life requires that desires be different, since the fields of life are many. This person's desire lies in one thing, and that person's desire lies in another. You see two close friends who are inseparable, sharing their food and drink, and nothing divides them; but when they go to buy something, their desires diverge. Likewise, one differing desire serves another differing desire. Those who differ, for instance, in the design of things, serve the difference of tastes and desires. Therefore they say: "Disagreement is the very essence of agreement, and agreement is the very essence of disagreement."

We have given a simple example of this: suppose you entered a restaurant, and you prefer, for instance, the chicken thigh, and someone else likewise prefers it, and it happens that there is only one thigh in the restaurant. There is no doubt that you will disagree over it. So you agreed at the start only to disagree at the end. But if your desires differ, this difference will in the end produce agreement: you will take the thigh, and the other will take the breast. This, then, is a disagreement that leads to agreement, and an agreement that leads to disagreement.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god...﴾ (al-Furqan 25:43). Desire is this: that there be a matter in which the face of the truth is clear, yet you turn away from it while you know it, not that you are ignorant of it.

Therefore the scholars say: the bane of opinion is desire. Opinion may be correct, but desire bends it wherever the person wills. And we have said that there is no clearer proof of this than that a man among them would walk and find a stone more beautiful than the stone he worshipped, so he would cast away the god he worshipped to take this one that is more beautiful than it, and make it a god. So his desire, in the beauty of the stone, overcame him, and it became a god.

The orientalists have stopped at His saying concerning the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Nor does he speak out of desire.﴾ (al-Najm 53:3).

They say: how does God judge that His Messenger did not speak out of desire, when God has corrected some of what he said, such as His saying: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you...?﴾ (al-Tahrim 66:1).

And He said: ﴿May Allah pardon you! Why did you grant them leave until it became clear to you...?﴾ (al-Tawbah 9:43).

We must first define the meaning of desire. You are aware that there are two matters: the truth is clear in one of them, yet his desire inclines toward other than the truth. He (ﷺ) spoke because there was no actual case in which he knew the face of the truth; therefore he did not follow desire, but rather what his ijtihad (independent reasoning) reached.

Do you not see His saying to His Messenger (ﷺ) in the matter of his adoption of Zayd ibn Harithah: ﴿Call them by their fathers' names; that is more just in the sight of Allah...﴾ (al-Ahzab 33:5). The meaning of ascribing them to their fathers being more just is that the Messenger of Allah was not unjust; what he did was just, but the act of Allah is more just than it.

Thus the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, did not err His Messenger (ﷺ), and called his act justice, which is human justice fitting to what Zayd had of attachment to the Messenger of Allah and his preference for him over his own family; so the Messenger of Allah found no better reward for him than to adopt him.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Would you then be responsible for him?﴾ (al-Furqan 25:43): a guardian who undertakes to direct him, so that he might abandon his desire and follow the truth. As He, glorified is He, says elsewhere: ﴿You are not over them a controller.﴾ (al-Ghashiyah 88:22). And He says: ﴿Would you then compel people until they become believers?﴾ (Yunus 10:99). And He says: ﴿Your duty is only to convey...﴾ (al-Shura 42:48).

So the one who follows his desire until he has made it his god, you cannot compel to turn away from his desire, because desires differ. Some want to enjoy the effort of others, so they put their hands into people's pockets to steal from them; but is it easiest for him that people should do to him what he does to them? Thus one desire collides with another desire: which of them prevails? He prevails who judges without desire, neither for you nor against you; and the matter of the truth in itself exists only from Allah, exalted is He.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Or do you think that most of them hear or understand? They are only like livestock; rather, they are further astray in way.﴾

﴿They hear...﴾ (al-Furqan 44): that is, hearing with understanding and reflection. Had they heard and understood, the means would not have brought them to this extent. ﴿They are only like livestock...﴾ (al-Furqan 44): although livestock are subjected (to human use) and perform their function, and do not refrain from anything for which they were created. God has likened them to livestock, because livestock are not asked to hear guidance, since they are subjected; whereas the one who is asked to hear and be guided is the one who is free to act or not to act.

It is as if the Truthful, glorified is He, were saying: Do you suppose that most of them hear or understand? The word ﴿most of them...﴾ (al-Furqan 44) indicates that some of them do hear and understand. This is from the principle of probability: many of the Quraysh disbelievers opposed the Messenger of God, and the matter ended with them embracing Islam and their Islam becoming sound. So there were among them those who heard, and those who disbelieved yet understood. Therefore He said ﴿most of them...﴾ (al-Furqan 44): to safeguard this ruling and to take into account what would come of the faith of these few. This is precision in seeking the truth.

We have already mentioned the regret of the believers when they missed killing one of the chiefs of disbelief in battle; they would grieve intensely over that, not knowing that God's wisdom was storing them up for faith later on, among them Khalid ibn al-Walid, who afterwards became the Drawn Sword of God.

We have said that livestock have no part in the matter of guidance or misguidance, because they are subjected and have no choice. Therefore God struck the parable of them for the Jews: ﴿The likeness of those who were charged with the Torah and then did not bear it is as the likeness of a donkey carrying books...﴾ (al-Jumu'ah 5). The donkey's task is only to carry, whereas you, O Jew, your task is to carry and to apply. The donkey does not apply, because nothing was asked of it. Yet the animal knows its owner, knows its food, the place of its drink, knows its path and the place of its lodging, to the extent that one of them died upon the back of his mount, and the mount carried him on to his house.

So then: livestock understand and comprehend within the limits of the function God created them for, and they do not fall short in their function. As for the religious duty, they know it in their inner reality, but nothing is demanded of them now, because they have finished with this matter first, as the Most High said:

﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and feared it; and man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.﴾ (al-Ahzab 72).

So they chose to be driven by instinct and governed by it. Thus they have a choice, but they executed their choice all at once from the very beginning.

Take as an example the hoopoe, one of the creatures subjected by God to Solomon, peace be upon him, who says to him: ﴿I have encompassed what you have not encompassed, and I have brought you certain news from Sheba﴾ (al-Naml 22). What democracy is this which the hoopoe enjoyed with Solomon?! So then, even animals know this matter, though nothing is demanded of them, and animals cannot do anything except when it is bound to their instincts and within their capacity.

We have earlier struck the example of the donkey: if you want it to leap over a water channel, it looks at it; if it is within its capacity it leaps, and if it is beyond its capacity it backs off, and no matter how much you beat it, it will not advance, because by its instinct it knows that this is beyond its abilities. Man, however, may proceed to such a thing without reckoning his capacities, and so he throws himself into what has an unpraised outcome.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow? Had He willed, He would have made it still. Then We made the sun its guide.﴾

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, who created the signs in the universe, draws the attention of creation to them. It would have been expected that whoever sees them would take notice of them without needing to be alerted: when he sees a wonder of the wonders of the universe, he contemplates it. We have already given an example of this: a man whose ways have been cut off in a vast desert, with no companion and no life in it, and whose exertion has reached the point that he falls asleep. When he awakes he finds a table on which are the finest foods or drinks. By God, before his hand reaches out to the food, is it not expected of him to reflect on this food: who brought it, and prepared it in this form?

Thus, in the universe there are signs that should have drawn your attention, so that you would seek them out and the traces of their existence, all of them lofty signs beyond our capacities: the sun and the moon, the air and the rain, and so on. Yet God did not leave you to take notice on your own; rather He alerted you, drew your attention to Him and to these things, and pulled your attention towards them.

Here, the Truth, blessed and exalted, presents the signs and cosmic phenomena that man sees daily with routine: the philosopher sees them as the shepherd sees them, the elder sees them as the child sees them, each day in one unchanging order, scarcely turning to them.

He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Have you not considered...﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:45), i.e., have you not known, or have you not looked at the handiwork of your Lord ﴿how He extends the shadow. Had He willed, He would have made it still.(1) Then We made the sun its guide﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:45). Indeed we see the shadow. What is it? The shadow is when a dense object on the earth, such as a mountain, a building, a tree or the like, blocks the light of the sun, so that an area of shade appears in a place that is sunlit. The matter, therefore, concerns the sun and the earth on which we live.

We know that the earth is a sphere facing the sun: the side facing the sun is illuminated, and the other side is darkness. We do not say "shade" (ẓill) here. What is the difference between shadow (ẓill) and darkness (ẓalām)? They said: if the thing blocking the sun's light comes from the earth itself, it is darkness; if the blocking thing is something on the earth, it is shadow.

We see shadow at all times, and it is mentioned in several places in the Book of God. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be among shades and springs﴾ (Al-Mursalat 77:41).

And He says: ﴿And We will admit them to shade, extended﴾ (An-Nisa 4:57).

And He says: ﴿Have they not considered what things God has created, how their shadows incline...﴾ (An-Nahl 16:48).

Our Lord, blessed and exalted, alerts us to another function of shadow: it protects us from the sting and heat of the sun. Man advances in using shadow, making it, as God says, ﴿extended shade﴾ (An-Nisa 4:57), i.e., the shade itself is shaded. For example, they make a tent with two separate roofs so that the inside of the tent is not affected by the heat outside it.

Therefore you find the shade of a tree gentler than the shade of a wall or an awning, because the leaves of the tree shade one another; the shade comes to you from another shading thing, so under a tree you feel as if you were in an air-conditioned place, because the leaves block the heat of the sun while allowing the breeze to pass through, as the poet said describing a large tree:
It turns away the sun wherever it faces us,
blocking it, and gives leave to the breeze.
And He, exalted, says: ﴿And when We raised the mountain over them like a canopy...﴾ (Al-Araf 7:171).

When you contemplate this phenomenon at sunrise, you see that the dense object blocking the sun's light casts a shadow that stretches to the horizon, then it begins to shorten as the sun rises until it reaches its zenith at midday; then the shadow reverses with the sun's inclination toward the west and lengthens until it reaches the horizon.

The Truth, blessed and exalted, wants us to notice this phenomenon and to reflect upon it: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow...﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:45), i.e., at the time of sunrise. ﴿Had He willed, He would have made it still...﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:45): for the will of God is able to create a thing and its opposite; if He wills, He extends the shadow, and if He wills, He holds it still.

But it changes: it decreases at the beginning of the day and increases at its end, and whatever accepts increase accepts decrease, and increase or decrease is motion. Motion has two kinds: a leaping motion, like the motion of the minute hand of a clock, which moves by leaps, meaning a still moment passes over the moving thing and then it moves; do you perceive that in the motion of the hour hand? No, because it moves with a flowing motion, such that the parts of the motion are distributed over the parts of time.

We may illustrate this motion with the growth of a small child, whose growth you do not perceive while looking at him from the day of his birth; but if you are away from him for a period, you can notice that he has grown and that his form has changed, because his growth is distributed over periods of time; he does not grow all at once, but these are increments of growth gathered over many times, and you do not have the precise measure with which to notice a child's growth in a short period.

If we can carry out this motion in clocks, for example, then the Truth, blessed and exalted, produces it in the motion of the shadow and attributes it to Himself, because of its greatness; the shadow does not move by a mechanical motion like that which you see in a clock, but moves by the power of God.

God, glory be to Him, drew our attention to this phenomenon, not merely as a cosmic phenomenon that we see and wonder at, but because we will exploit it and benefit from it in many things.

The ancient Egyptians erected obelisks to regulate time by means of the shadow, and the Muslim Arabs made the sundial (mazwalah) to fix the hour by the movement of the sun. Today we see the simple farmer look at the shadow of something and tell you: "The time now is such-and-such," because he has become accustomed to measuring time by the shadow, although such an estimate is not precise, since the sun has many risings over the days of the year. Therefore, in one of the temples of the Pharaohs there is a temple with 365 openings, one of which the sun enters each day.

So: the shadow was of benefit to us in obelisks and sundials, and from them the Muslims moved on to making clocks; the first of them was the water-driven clock (al-sa'a al-daqqaqa), and they gifted one of them to Charlemagne, king of France, who said: "In it there is a devil." Such were the early Muslims.

As for His saying, exalted: ﴿Then We made the sun its guide﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:45): i.e., the light is what indicates the shadow.

1 That is, constant and settled, not abrogated by the sun; said by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/4914).

2 Natq: to lift a thing from its place, move it, and pull it. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/252). Ibn Abbas said: the angels lifted it over their heads. Sunayd ibn Dawud mentioned in his tafsir that God revealed to the mountain, so it was uprooted and rose into the sky until it was between their heads and the sky; Musa said to them: "Do you not see what my Lord, mighty and majestic, says? If you do not accept the Torah with what is in it, I will crush you with this." (Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/261).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 46:

﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal.﴾

Al-Haqq (the Truth), blessed and exalted is He, explains the slow movement of the shadow, saying: ﴿a gradual withdrawal﴾ (al-Furqan). You will never perceive it, because in every moment of time there is movement, so time, however brief, is never free of movement. But you do not have the measure by which you could perceive the slowness of this movement.

His saying: ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us...﴾ (al-Furqan) is evidence that the matter is not mechanics; rather, it is by the self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah) of Allah, exalted is He. Thus it is as if Allah, glorified is He, says: O My servants, sleep with your eyes full, for your Lord is the Sustainer (Qayyum) over your welfare and does not sleep.

And the people of gnosis (ahl al-ma'rifah) derive secrets from the phenomenon of the shadow. They see that the shadows of lofty, towering things submit to Allah, exalted is He, and prostrate upon the earth, despite their being high and lofty, as He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and their shadows [too], in the mornings and the evenings﴾ (al-Ra'd, 15).

And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Each has known its prayer and its glorification﴾ (al-Nur, 41). So the shadow has a slow movement which none knows except Allah, because you cannot perceive the extent of its smallness. Therefore we have said regarding the haba' (floating dust-motes): it is the ultimate limit of what can be visibly fragmented.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 25, verse 47:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And it is He who made for you the night as a garment, and sleep as rest, and made the day a resurrection.﴾

﴿The night…﴾ (al-Furqan): He means the darkness, not the shade. It is darkness that prevents the light. Beware lest you think that darkness is the opposite of light, and then try to abolish the darkness with a light of your own making. This is the calamity of modern civilization, which has made the night into day.

Scholars have recently become aware of the extent of the harm that rays cause to human health. For this reason the noble hadith says: "Extinguish the lamps when you go to sleep" (1). Light has its function during your waking movement, but at the hour of your sleep and rest it has no purpose; rather, it is harmful at this time.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, reminds us of the favour of night and day, saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then hear? Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then see?﴾ (al-Qasas) (2).

So the night has a function, and the day has a function, which the Truth, glory be to Him, clarifies here in His saying: ﴿And it is He who made for you the night as a garment…﴾ (al-Furqan), i.e., a covering, just as a garment covers the body. Sleep is a natural restraint that overpowers the living being; it is not a restraint of choice.

Therefore you notice that if you wish to sleep at a time other than the time of sleep, you grow tired and exhausted; but if sleep comes to you, you settle and calm down. From here they said: "Sleep is a heavy guest: if you seek it, it distresses you; if it seeks you, it gives you rest."

Therefore, when sleep seeks you, you sleep to the full of your eyelids, and even on pebbles sleep overcomes you and you sleep, as though sleep were saying to you: "Be still and rest." You are no longer fit for movement. But whoever struggles against this nature, and takes, for example, pills that help him stay awake, will sleep for two nights after one night of wakefulness, and the movement of one who struggles against sleep comes out agitated and unbalanced.

So it is incumbent upon you, then, to submit to this nature with which Allah created you, and to yield to sleep if it insists upon you, and not to be arrogant, so that you rise in the morning vigorous and resume the movement of your life strong and fit for work and giving.

For the Sufis there is a subtle observation concerning sleep, based on the fact that the whole of existence, that which is not chosen, glorifies its Lord, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿Each knows its prayer and its glorification…﴾ (al-Nur) (41). Accordingly, the atoms of the disbeliever are in themselves believing; they are pained and enraged that their owner is disobedient or unbelieving, yet they obey him while disliking his deed. The proof is that they will testify against him on the Day of Resurrection. If they were subjugated to his desires in this world, they will be freed from this desire in the Hereafter.

The tongue is subjugated to its owner: if he wills, it utters the two testimonies; if he wills, it utters the word of disbelief, because it is subdued to his will. But on the Resurrection there is no will except that of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He.

In sleep these limbs and these atoms are relieved from the evil deeds of their owner and his sins; they rest from his wretchedness and from his compelling them to disobey Allah. Thus sleep is an energetic restraint: the human being is no longer fit for movement, nor for peaceful coexistence with his limbs. His sins and disobediences have multiplied until the limbs have been straitened by them, so sleep comes to give them rest.

We see this phenomenon, for example, in the season of Hajj: the pilgrim tells you, "It is enough for me to sleep an hour or two in the day." Why? Because sins are few in this place, so your limbs are at rest and in harmony with you, and do not compel you to sleep. But the disobedient person is not satisfied with sleeping ten hours, because his limbs and organs are tired and oppressed by his actions.

With this we explain that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sleep with his eyes while his heart did not sleep (3). That is because his limbs (ﷺ) accompanied him in the best companionship, for they were in constant, continuous obedience; so how could they compel him to sleep?

The Creator, mighty and majestic is He, deals with people according to the general meaning: souls are always inclined to evil and prone to wrongdoing; therefore the energy is exhausted and the limbs are exhausted. It is as though Allah, exalted is He, wishes to establish a truce for coexistence between you and your limbs: sleep, so that you may wake up energetic.

And the meaning of ﴿and sleep as rest…﴾ (al-Furqan): "sabt" means cutting off. So the meaning of ﴿sabatan…﴾ (al-Furqan) is: a cutting off of movement, not a permanent cessation, but a cutting off that is resumed for a better movement and a stronger, healthier body. He who spends a night awake rises from his sleep tired and agitated, unlike one who made the time of sleep for sleep; for the Creator, mighty and majestic is He, made your sleep at night proportional to your movement by day. If you want balanced, energetic and strong movement, then sleep in proportion to this movement.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and made the day a resurrection﴾ (al-Furqan): "nushur" is like "shukur": ﴿We only feed you for the sake of Allah; we do not desire from you reward or gratitude﴾ (al-Insan) (9), i.e., thanks. Likewise "nushur" means "nashr" (dispersal), and "nashr" means setting out across the earth in movement, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then disperse in the land and seek of Allah's bounty…﴾ (al-Jumu'ah) (10).

1. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (5624), and Ahmad in his Musnad (3/388), from Jabir ibn Abdullah; the wording is that of al-Bukhari.
2. Al-sarmad: that which is lasting and does not cease; and al-sarmad: the permanence of time, whether of night or day. (Lisan al-Arab, root s-r-m-d).
3. A hadith agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3569), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (738), Book of the Prayer of Travellers, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Aisha, my eyes sleep, but my heart does not sleep."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 48:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿It is He who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water.﴾

We have said: when the winds come in this form, in the plural, they indicate goodness, and when they come in the singular, they come with evil. When you look at the high mountains and at the skyscrapers, you say: what holds these high buildings up so that they do not lean? What holds them is the air that surrounds them from every side, and if you removed the air from one of their sides, they would collapse immediately.

So the wind comes from here, and from here, and from here. It is many winds that are suitable and do not corrupt, and they produce this balance that we see in the universe. As for the wind that comes from one direction, it is destructive and annihilating, as the Exalted said: ﴿As for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind﴾ (al-Haqqah 69:6).

And He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Rather, it is what you were hastening for: a wind in which is a painful punishment﴾ (al-Ahqaf 46:24).

As for the meaning of ﴿bushran﴾ (al-Furqan 25:48): it is with a sukun on the shin, although originally it is bushran, like rusul; when it was lightened it became bushran. Al-bushra is the announcement of what gladdens before its time, so one does not say yubashshir except for good. The Arab, when the winds passed over him, would know how far he was from the rain, and would judge the coming of rain by the movement of the soft winds that caress his cheek.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿before His mercy﴾ (al-Furqan 25:48): it is said: "bayna yadayk" meaning: in front of you. What is meant here is the rain that precedes the mercy of God.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿and We send down from the sky pure water﴾ (al-Furqan 25:48). "Sama'" (sky) has a linguistic meaning and a legal meaning. Linguistically it is everything that is above you; legally it is this lofty sky, which consists of seven heavens. But does the rain descend from the sky or from the direction of the sky?

The rain descends from the clouds, from the direction of the sky, and the clouds originally come from the earth as a result of the process of evaporation that gathers in the layers of the atmosphere, as the Glorified said:

﴿Do you not see that God drives the clouds gently, then joins them together, then makes them a heap, and you see the rain coming out from their midst, and He sends down from the sky, from mountains in it of hail...﴾ (al-Nur 24:43).

So the mercy of God is the water from which God created every living thing.

As for His saying: ﴿pure water﴾ (al-Furqan 25:48): "tahur" is water that is pure in itself and purifying to others. The water with which you perform ablution is pure and purifying; but after you have performed ablution with it, it is pure in itself yet no longer purifying to others. The water of the sky is pure and purifying, because it is clarified and distilled, and distilled water is the purest water.

In addition, water is the sustenance of life; from it we drink, and with it we water crops, animals and birds. Water gives you life and gives you purity.

1 "Al-rih al-sarsar": extremely cold; it was also said: extremely loud. (Lisan al-Arab, root: s-r-r).
2 "Azja al-shay'": he drives it gently; so "yuzji sahaban" means: he drives the cloud to wherever he wills. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/284; Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4825).
3 Regarding "al-wadq" there are two opinions:
The first: that it is lightning, said by Abu al-Ashhab al-'Uqayli.
The second: that it is rain, said by the majority. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4826). Al-Suyuti also mentioned both opinions in (al-Durr al-Manthur 6/211): the first from Abu Bujayla, attributed by him to Ibn Abi Hatim, and the second from al-Dahhak and Mujahid, in Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Abi Shaybah.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿That We may give life thereby to a dead land, and give drink to many of the cattle and people We have created.﴾

The words of the Exalted: ﴿a dead land....﴾ (al-Furqan): that is, the land of a dead town. There is a distinction between "dead" (mayyit) and "dead" (mayyit): the mayyit is the one who has actually died, and the mayyit is the one whose affair is heading toward death, even while he is still alive. Among this is the saying of the Exalted, addressing His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed you will die, and indeed they will die﴾ (al-Zumar).

The dead land is the barren land, devoid of vegetation. When water descends upon it, He gives it life with plants, as in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And you see the earth barren, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and produces from every beautiful pair﴾ (al-Hajj).

As for His saying, ﴿and give drink to... many of the cattle and people We have created﴾ (al-Furqan): it is said "saqahu" and "asqahu." Asqahu means: he prepared for him that from which he may draw water, even if he does not drink now. But saqahu means: he handed him what he drinks. Among this is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And their Lord gave them to drink a pure drink﴾ (al-Insan).

As for rain, He says, glorified is He: ﴿And We gave you to drink of it...﴾ (al-Hijr). That is: We prepared it for your watering, if you wish to be watered.

And the meaning of ﴿wa-anasiyy...﴾ (al-Furqan): it is the plural of insan (human being), and its original form was anasin, which was lightened to anasi.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 50:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq), glorified is He, says:

﴿And We have certainly distributed it among them that they might remember, but most of the people refused except disbelief.﴾

Tasrif (تصريف): transformation and change; the meaning is that We turned it from here to there. And despite all these lessons and signs, ﴿most of the people refused except disbelief﴾ (al-Furqan): the disbelievers in the signs of God are many; they pay no heed to the signs of God, even after knowledge has advanced and human civilization has progressed, and people have come to know many of the signs.

So God, blessed and exalted, directs the rain to one land in abundance, and if He wills, drought and barrenness befall it until their crops and livestock die. Therefore, the matter is not one of a cold climate or of abundant rainfall; rather, the matter is the will of the Creator and the will of the Truth.

1 Qatada... ʿIkrimah said: "It means those who say: 'We have been given rain by such-and-such a star (nawʾ)'." This which ʿIkrimah said is as is authenticated in the hadith recorded in Sahih Muslim from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he said to his companions one day following a rain that had fallen on them during the night: "Do you know what your Lord said?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "In the morning, among My servants, there are those who believe in Me and those who disbelieve. As for the one who says, 'We have been given rain by the grace of God and His mercy,' he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the star. But as for the one who says, 'We have been given rain by such-and-such a star,' he is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the star." (Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/321)..

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 25, verse 51:

﴿And if We had willed, We would have sent a warner to every town.﴾

The Exalted and Blessed One wishes to bestow a favour upon His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying to him: The matter is not that We lack messengers, so that We would have to send one messenger to all mankind and for all time. Rather, We are able to lighten the burden upon you and send a messenger to every town. But He sends one messenger and gives him a capacity that can bear all of this.

Then the Exalted says:

﴿So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it, a great striving.﴾ (25:52)

That is: since We have gathered for you all the powers and entrusted you with the general message in every time and every place, you must take the stance suited to this mission. ﴿So do not obey the disbelievers...﴾ (25:52): even if they dangle before you kingship, wealth, or status and honor. Know that what Allah has prepared for you and stored up for you is far beyond all of this.

When the Almighty says to His Messenger ﷺ ﴿So do not obey the disbelievers...﴾ (25:52), He is excusing him before them, for the Messenger carries out the commands of Allah.

The prohibition to the Messenger from obeying the disbelievers does not mean that he ﷺ would obey them. This is like the saying of the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, believe...﴾ (4:136). How can faith be demanded of those who have been addressed as believers? It is an attainment of what is already attained (taḥṣīl ḥāṣil). They said: the meaning is: you have believed before I said this word to you, and I say it to you now so that you continue in a new faith alongside the first faith, and beware lest faith be loosened from you. Thus, when the existing is commanded, what is intended is the continuation of its existence.

As for the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And strive against them with it...﴾ (25:52): that is, with what has come to you of the Qur'an. ﴿...a great striving.﴾ (25:52). Know that by Allah's command you will prevail over them. Do not say that there is a current of polytheism, disbelief, and faith; I will give you a cosmic example regarding the most important thing in your life, which is water.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 53:

﴿And it is He who let loose the two seas: this one sweet, fresh, and this one salty, bitter; and He placed between them a barrier and an inviolable partition.﴾

This verse continues the mention of some of God's signs in the cosmos, which draw the attention of the obstinate deniers who opposed the Messenger of God. God had earlier mentioned the shade, the night, the winds, and so on. Thus, whenever He mentions their obstinacy, He brings a cosmic sign to draw their attention to the fact that they have been heedless of God's signs. Their disputation with the Messenger of God shows that they have paid no attention to any of this. Therefore He mentioned a cosmic sign from God's signs that is visible to all and repeated, and upon which there is an evidence that stands until the Day of Resurrection. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it is He who let loose the two seas...﴾ (al-Furqan: 53).

Al-marj (مرج): the open pasture, or the common grazing land where the shepherd lets his flock roam freely as it wishes.

So the meaning of ﴿let loose the two seas...﴾ (al-Furqan: 53) is: He made the sweet and the salty to flow, each as it wills. Thus you find the salty seas and oceans, which constitute three-quarters of the dry land, have no regular geometric shape; rather you find them winding and twisting. Look, for example, at the Gulf of Mexico or the Gulf of Aqaba, as if the water moves according to its (own) whim and without order, so that it does not form a rectangle, a square, or a circle.

Likewise the rivers that are born of the rains upon the high mountains: you see them, when they gather and flow as they wish, twisting and winding, because water cuts its course through the easy places; if it meets a small obstacle, it deviates here or there in order to complete its path. Look, for example, at the winding of the Nile at Qena.

So: sweet or salty water flows according to its own whim, and the matter is not "mechanics," nor is it regular like what man cuts, which comes out straight.

We notice this phenomenon, for example, when a person relieves himself in the open: the urine cuts a channel for itself in the place that does not hinder it, and if it meets a pebble, for example, it deviates from it as if choosing its path according to its own whim.

The word "sea" (al-bahr) is commonly applied to both the salty and the sweet, by way of prevalence (taghlib), just as we say "the two suns" (al-shamsan) for the sun and the moon.

The "let loose of the two seas" is a cosmic sign that indicates the power of God. Water, with its known property of seeking low places (istitrad), i.e., it flows toward the low regions, the salty and the sweet flow together without one mixing with the other; and if they were to mix, both would be spoiled. For if the sweet were mixed with the salty, it would become unfit for drinking, and if the salty were mixed with the sweet, the salty would be spoiled. God created it at a certain degree of saltiness such that it preserves it from corruption and keeps it from becoming stagnant (āsin).

Thus, if you confine sweet water in one place, it becomes stagnant (ya'sin) and changes, whereas the sea, God has prepared it to be the storehouse of water in the cosmos and the source of evaporation from which the rivers are formed. Therefore He preserved it, and placed between it and the sweet water a peaceful coexistence, such that neither of them oppresses the other despite their adjacency.

As for His words, exalted is He: ﴿this one sweet, fresh...﴾ (al-Furqan: 53): i.e., excessively sweet and palatable. From this word they named the river Euphrates (al-Furat) for the sweetness of its water. The intended meaning of "al-Furat" is not that the water is like the water of the Euphrates River, because the word was first established, and then the river was named by it; that is because the Qur'an is the eternal speech of God.

﴿and this one salty, bitter...﴾ (al-Furqan: 53): i.e., intensely salty. Nevertheless, fish and aquatic animals live in it and feed on it just as they feed on sweet water, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and from each you eat fresh flesh and extract ornaments you wear...﴾ (Fatir: 12).

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿and He placed between them a barrier and an inviolable partition﴾ (al-Furqan: 53): al-barzakh (البرزخ): a thing between two things. The original meaning of the word barzakh is the dry land that separates two waters; if the water is between two lands, it is a gulf (khalij).

﴿and an inviolable partition﴾ (al-Furqan: 53): al-hijr (الحجر) is the barrier that prevents the sweet and the salty from mixing, and the hijr itself is "maḥjūr," as an intensification in prohibiting the mixing of the two waters, as in His saying: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾ (al-Isra': 45).

And like His saying: ﴿a constant shade﴾ (al-Nisa': 57).

1 Marj: He released them and let one overflow into the other. Said by Mujahid. Ibn 'Arafa said: i.e., he mixed them, so they meet. Al-Azhari said: marj al-bahrayn: he left them free between them. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/4934).
2 Al-ujaj: intensely salty brine. Ajja al-ma': its saltiness intensified. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/7).
3 Asina al-ma' ya'sinu: its smell changed, so it is asin (stagnant). (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/20).

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿It is He who created man from water and made him [a being with] lineage and marriage. And your Lord is ever Competent.﴾ (25:54)

And concerning water in a general verse, Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We made from water every living thing....﴾ (21:30). That is, everything that has life is from water, not that water is inside everything. The meaning is: ﴿every living thing﴾ (21:30), i.e., everything described as living. Water, therefore, is a sign of life. For this reason, when scientists wish to destroy microbes or viruses, they develop a medicine that separates them from water, and so they die.

As for man, whom Allah has honored and made the highest of creatures, Allah created him from water: ﴿And it is He who created man from water....﴾ (25:54). In another place He, glorified is He, says: ﴿So let man look at what he was created from. He was created from a gushing fluid, emerging from between the backbone and the ribs﴾ (86:5–7). This is the fluid that has a particular property, namely semen, concerning which Allah says: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted? Then he became a clinging clot, and He formed [him] and proportioned [him]﴾ (75:37–38).

And "al-bashar" means humankind, ﴿and made him [a being with] lineage and marriage....﴾ (25:54). So from water Allah created humankind, and they are of two kinds: male and female. The word "nasab" (lineage) signifies the male, and "sihr" (marriage/in-law relation) signifies the female, because lineage means the transmission of the lower from the higher through the male line, so that a person remains "so-and-so son of so-and-so son of so-and-so..." and so on.

Lineage comes through the male side. As for the female, no lineage arises from her; rather, there is only affinity (musahara), when a man marries my daughter or I marry his daughter; they call him a "sihr" (in-law).

Therefore the poet said:
"Indeed the mothers of the people are but vessels,
newly made, while the noble lineages have fathers."

So from the greatness of the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, is that He created from water these two things, as He said elsewhere: ﴿And made of him the two mates, the male and the female﴾ (75:39). Scientists have recently concluded that the female ovum has no role in determining the sex of the fetus, and that it is nothing but a host for the microbe coming from the man's semen.

This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted? Then he became a clinging clot, and He formed [him] and proportioned [him], and made of him the two mates, the male and the female﴾ (75:37–39). The male and the female both come from the semen, and what scientists now call the "X" and the "XY." The sperm cell that comes out of the man includes some that carry the male determinant and some that carry the female determinant; then a process of selection takes place for the strongest that can fertilize the ovum.

This phenomenon is clear in bees, where the queen lays eggs and only the strongest of the males fertilizes them; for this reason the queen flies at high altitudes. Why? To select the strongest of the males.

Likewise, the microbe descends from the man, and the strongest of them is the one that can get ahead to the woman's ovum. If the one specific to maleness gets there first, it is a male; if the one specific to femaleness gets there first, it is a female. And the Truthful, glorified is He, said: ﴿He who created and proportioned, and He who measured and guided﴾ (87:2–3).

By this cosmic sign in the creation of man we answer those who like to say that man was created by chance. If man is male and female, with common characteristics, the same organs and the same constituents, yet the male differs in the reproductive system and so does the female, can this be attributed to chance?

It is well known that chance is the enemy of consistency. If the male came by chance, and the female came by chance too, is it by chance that they should meet in a specific manner, and that this meeting should bear fruit in maleness and femaleness? So the matter is not a coincidence; rather, it is a purpose intended by the Creator, mighty and majestic is He.

Then He, glorified is He, says at the end of the verse: ﴿And your Lord is ever Competent﴾ (25:54). He mentioned power here because this is a subtle matter that does not occur except by the power of Allah, the Exalted.

The Arabs, even before the revelation of the Qur'an, were instinctively aware of this process. Thus the wife of Abu Hamza rebuked him because he had left her and married another, since she had not borne him a male. She says:
"What is wrong with Abu Hamza that he does not come to us angry? Is it that we do not bear sons? By Allah, that is not in our hands; we are like the land for those who plant in us; we give them what we were given."

And this matter, which the ancient Arab perceived, was not known to science until the twentieth century.

(1) al-tara'ib: the bones of the chest (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/99). Ibn 'Abbas said: "These are the tara'ib," and he placed his hand on his chest. Also from him: the tara'ib are the place of the necklace on a woman's chest. (Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4/498).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 25, verse 55:

After this cosmic sign (verse 54), Allah, glorified and exalted, returns to addressing them once more, so that their hearts may be softened. Al-Haqq, blessed and exalted, attends to them sometimes with counsel and sometimes by showing His signs in the universe.

﴿And they worship besides Allah that which neither benefits them nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever a helper [of Satan] against his Lord.﴾

That is: is it fitting for them, after We have made all these signs clear to them, that they should turn to other than Allah and direct their worship to Him?

As for His saying, ﴿that which neither benefits them nor harms them⦆ (Al-Furqan). Some hold that these deities do not benefit but do harm. We say to them: they neither benefit nor harm. What harms is the true God, from whom they have turned away to worship other than Him. The meaning here is: ﴿that which neither benefits them﴾ (Al-Furqan): if they worship Him; ﴿nor harms them﴾ (Al-Furqan): if they disbelieve in Him and abandon Him.

The Qur'an calls their conduct toward these deities "worship," and they themselves say: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in nearness﴾ (Az-Zumar, 3).

So they have affirmed worship for them. Worship is the obedience of the worshipper to the worshipped in what it commands and what it forbids. So what have the idols commanded them, and what have they forbidden them? The word "worship" here is therefore inaccurate. They worshipped these deities only because they have no commands and impose no obligations, so their religiosity is a "comfortable" (fanṭaziyya) religiosity.

How easy it is to worship a god who does not command you or forbid you. What people dislike in true religion is that it is an obligation and a responsibility: do this, do not do that.
