Therefore you see those who are lax with themselves among the creatures of Allah wishing that this religion were a lie. Why? So that they may walk according to their desires and do what pleases them. Likewise we have seen the impostors who claimed prophethood, beginning with Musaylima and Sajah¹, and how they drew people to them. They drew them by lightening the commands and simplifying the religion. When zakat became burdensome for some, they dropped it from their accounts and exempted the people from it… and so on.

For every age there are impostors suited to the era in which they live. In our present age there are impostors who lighten religion for you and bend it to people's desires and appetites, so they see no harm in mixing of the sexes, and no harm in a woman wearing whatever clothing she wishes… and so on through these matters.

Then He, glorified, says: ﴿and the disbeliever is ever a helper against his Lord﴾ (Al-Furqan).

Al-Zahir (the helper, ẓahīr) is the one who assists, as in His saying, ﴿…and if you two support one another against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibril and the righteous among the believers, and the angels after that are [his] helpers﴾ (At-Tahrim, 4).

In the past, people carried loads on their backs before the invention of carrying machines, and even now we see porters (al-shayyalin) carrying heavy weights on their backs, and they sew for themselves a "back-pad" (ẓahriyya) that they wear on their backs to bear the load while carrying. When one of them wants to help another, he says to him: "Give me your back." So "back" (ẓahr) in this sense carries the meaning of support.

Also, ẓahr implies height, as in His saying about the barrier built by Dhu al-Qarnayn: ﴿So they were unable to scale it, nor were they able to pierce it﴾ (Al-Kahf, 97). That is: they were unable to climb over it.

But how can the disbeliever be a helper against Allah? They said: because he commits sin and takes as an example in it, which people imitate. Had he been obedient, he would have been an example of good and a model of righteousness. The disbeliever is thus an example of evil and an example of corruption, and he is the devil of mankind who conceals the devil of the jinn who disobeyed his Lord and refused to prostrate to Adam.

And he threatened his offspring when he said: ﴿He said: My Lord, because You have sent me astray, I will surely adorn [evil] for them on earth and mislead them all﴾ (Al-Hijr, 39).

Each of the devils of the jinn and the devils of mankind seeks the aid of the self, empowering it over its owner until it brings him to ruin. When a person listens to the call of Satan, whether the devil of mankind or the devil of the jinn, and obeys him by committing transgression, he has helped him against Allah. The correct meaning is: in disobedience to Allah.

Also, ẓahīr is applied to one whom you place behind your back, not caring for him and not paying attention to him. From this is the Arab saying: "Do not make my need [something] behind your back," meaning: place it before your eyes; do not trample it behind your back.²

So both meanings are permissible: ẓahīr meaning helper. It is as if the Exalted Lord is saying to His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Know, O Muhammad, that the disbeliever is a helper against Allah. So stand against him in ambush and strive against him as much as you can." Thus He, exalted, rouses His Messenger to take this stance and encourages him to be wary of his enemy and alert.

Or: ẓahīr meaning one who is disregarded, and this is a reassurance to the Messenger of Allah: the disbeliever is insignificant before Allah, so do not be concerned about their schemes.

And their saying "Do not make my need a back" means: do not forget it. From this is His saying: ﴿and you took Him behind your backs, as something cast away﴾ (Hud, 92), and it is your contempt for a man's need. And "he made me a back" means: he cast me off.

Then the Truthful Lord says:

﴿And We did not send you except as a bringer of good news and a warner.﴾

It is true that Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh upon them…﴾ (al-Tawbah 9:73). However, this does not mean that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ should destroy himself in calling them, and suffer the utmost pain because of their lack of faith; for the duty of the Messenger is only to convey (al-balagh). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ grieved over the condition of his people, until his Lord addressed him saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their footsteps, if they do not believe in this message.﴾ (al-Kahf 18:6).

Allah did not command him to strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites except to spur him on, so that he would leave no effort unexerted with them. Otherwise, to me you are a bringer of good news and a warner. ﴿And We did not send you except as a bringer of good news…﴾ (al-Furqan 25:56): that is, of good before its time, so that people turn their attention to its means. ﴿…and a warner﴾ (al-Furqan 25:56): that is, of evil before its time, so that people beware of it and avoid its causes and means.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 25, verse 57:

Then the Lord of Might directs His Prophet and Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it, except that whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.﴾ (25:57)

In another verse, He the Exalted says: ﴿Or do you ask them for a wage, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ (52:40)

That is: unable to pay the price, because they are stingy and have hardness (kazzazah)(1)? Or they do not want to take anything out of their pockets that you would benefit from? Even though you did not ask them for a wage. Does this mean that the Prophet was supposed to ask them for a wage?

They said: Yes, because when a person offers another person something beneficial, it is incumbent on him to pay him a wage, by the requirement of exchange and reciprocity. It is as if the Prophet (ﷺ) were saying to them: I have offered you a favour for which it would be expected that I have a wage from you, but I do not want a wage from you, and the matter is from me as a bounty.

And what is the ajr (wage)? Ajr: a reward set against a work; and thaman (price): a reward set against an ownership. The value of this reward varies according to the hardship of the work, the length of its time, the skill of the worker in what the work requires, and the risks that the work entails.

So each of these matters raises the value of the wage. For example, when you travel you need a porter (shayyal) to carry your bags for you, and you give him a wage that corresponds to his effort. If you hire a car and travel a distance with it, the wage will certainly increase, because it has taken more effort and time. If you need, for instance, a plumber to fix something for you, you will see the hardship in this work, and you will not be stingy with him more than with those before him.

Perhaps the work in your view is simple and does not take much time, but it requires skill. This skill is not the product of the moment; rather it is effort and the result of factors of learning and experience until its possessor reached this skill.

So the engineer, for example, who designs your house in an hour or two, yet asks for a large sum—why? Because he does not receive a wage for this time, but for many years of study, effort and acquisition, until he reached this skill.

Therefore: every wage is measured by the work that corresponds to it, and it accords with what the work requires of time, effort, hardship, risk and skill... etc.

If that is the case, then look at the work of the Messenger and the extent of your benefit from his message. Look at the method that came to you with him, and how it gives you rest with yourselves, gives you rest with society, gives you rest with your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and protects you from the evils of your own selves and from the evils of all people.

So: the Messenger has a great work and tremendous effort. If you were to set a wage for him, it would likewise be great. When a person hires, for example, a guard to watch over him at night, how much does he pay him? The Prophet brings you a method that guards and protects you in yourself, in your wealth, in your honour and in everything you possess, and it does not protect you from a particular group but from all people.

Indeed, the protection of God's method for you is not confined to this world; it extends to the Hereafter, protecting you there with a protection that is extended and has no end. If you were to set a wage for this protection, how much would it be?

Rather, I say to you: I do not want a wage—not out of dislike for wages, but because you, O human, cannot estimate this work or set a wage upon it. The One who estimates it is my Lord who sent me, and you, O servant, however much wage you offer me for it, it is little.

And we recount the story of the good man whom we met in Algeria, who stood on the road signalling to a car to carry him. We stopped and opened the door for him to ride with us, and before he got in he said: "How much?"—meaning the fare. My companion said to him: "For God's sake." The man said: "Then it is very expensive." This is the meaning in His saying, Exalted: ﴿My wage is only upon God...﴾ (11:29).

And in another place He, glorified, says: ﴿My wage is only upon God, and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims.﴾ (10:72) What is the connection between the wage and ﴿and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾ (10:72)?

The Muslim ought to do the work not for the one for whom he works, but to do it for God, to take the wage that corresponds to this work from His hand, the Exalted. But if he takes it from the one he works for, then he is like the one who "did it so that it would be said, and it has been said," and the matter is finished, and perhaps he will not even be thanked for his work.

For this reason this statement was conveyed on the tongues of all the Messengers: ﴿And I ask you no wage for it...﴾ (26:109). And there is no verse in which an apparent wage is requested except this verse we are dealing with: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it, except that whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.﴾ (25:57)

And His saying, Exalted: ﴿Except the affection among kin...﴾ (42:23).

And the meaning of ﴿except that whoever wills may take a path to his Lord﴾ (25:57): that is, a path to reward, and a path to wage, through striving in the way of God, or charity to the poor... etc.

And His saying: ﴿except whoever wills...﴾ (25:57) indicates choice in paying the wage. The Messenger takes nothing except voluntarily, and the wage is: ﴿that he take a path to his Lord﴾ (25:57), through striving and righteous deeds. So the Messenger's wage is working for others, so that you take the wage from God; the Messenger takes nothing for himself.

And we notice in the verses on wage that it came once as ﴿ajran...﴾ (6:90), and once as ﴿min ajr...﴾ (25:57). Some hold that "min" here is superfluous, but this should not be said of the words of God; it is a fault to accuse the speech of God of having surplus, for every letter in it has its meaning.

We have previously given an example for this "min" by saying: "ma indi mal" and "ma indi min mal." The first negates that you have wealth that is of account, though you may have a little of it; but the second statement means the negation of wealth absolutely, from the outset of what is called wealth. So which of them is more emphatic in negation? Thus here "min" conveys generality.

For this reason He, Exalted, says: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment, when the payment of your Lord is better...﴾ (23:72). Why? Because He will give you and reward you according to His measure, and in accordance with His generosity and bounty, which does not run out; whereas a human will give you according to his own measure and within his limited capacities.

Another point on this matter is in Surah al-Shu'ara', which is the most abundant of the surahs in mentioning the question of wage, for it deals with the procession of the Messengers, mentioning eight of them: Musa, Harun, Ibrahim, Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb.

You notice that all these Messengers said: ﴿My wage is only upon the Lord of the worlds﴾ (26:109), except Ibrahim and Musa, peace be upon them, who did not say this word. Why?

They said: Because when you ask a wage for work you have done, there is nothing that obliges you to work for him for free; for you do not take a wage if you do something, for example, out of courtesy to a friend. Likewise Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when he first called to faith, called his uncle Azar, and from such a person no wage is asked. And Musa, peace be upon him, when he first called, called Pharaoh, who had embraced him and raised him in his house; and if he had asked him for a wage, he would have said: "What wage, when I raised you?" ... etc.

The other verse concerning the exception is His saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it, except affection among the near of kin...﴾ (42:23). So it is as if affection among kin were the wage of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for his message. But which kin: the kin of the Prophet, or your kin?

There is no doubt that the Prophet, who makes the love of a relative for a relative and his care for him his wage—meaning by "kin" all the believers—as his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, said of him: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves...﴾ (33:6).

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 25, verse 58:

﴿And rely upon the Living One, who does not die, and glorify Him with His praise. And sufficient is He as Knower of the sins of His servants.﴾

Almighty Allah reassures His Messenger ﷺ: "O Muhammad, do not be concerned with the multitude of the disbelievers, their scheming against you, or their cooperation with the devils of mankind and jinn. These will fall away and die, either at your hands or by a punishment from Allah. And even if they were to live on, their strength and stratagems will not overcome the power of Allah the Exalted and His plotting. And even if they rely upon idols that neither harm nor benefit, you should rely upon Allah: ﴿And rely upon the Living One, who does not die...﴾ (al-Furqan 25:58)."

The sensible person relies only upon one he trusts and whose help is guaranteed, and who will agree with you in everything you want. But what is the benefit of relying upon someone who will settle your interest for you, only for you to hear of his death in the morning?

It is as if Almighty Allah wishes to advise His creation: if you want to rely upon someone, then rely upon one who benefits you and does not abandon you, upon one who remains faithful to the covenant with you and does not forsake you, upon one whom nothing in the earth or heaven can overpower. This is shrewdness.

But what is the benefit of relying upon one who has no life? And even if He had everlasting life, you cannot guarantee that His heart will not turn against you.

﴿And glorify Him with His praise...﴾ (al-Furqan 25:58): "Glorify" (sabbih) means to declare Him free of imperfection (tanzih), and you place this tanzih within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him...﴾ (al-Shura 42:11). Allah has existence, and you have existence, but His existence is not like your attributes. Allah has acts, and you have acts, but His acts are not like your acts.

So: declare Allah free of imperfection in His essence, in His attributes, and in His acts, far above resemblance to creation. Since the Truth, glory be to Him, is free of imperfection in His essence, attributes and acts, you rely upon a God upon whom the factors of change never come.

This declaration of Allah's transcendence, and this greatness and majesty of His, glory be to Him, are for your own benefit, O human. It is to your advantage that there be no likeness to Allah, neither in His existence, nor in His permanence, nor in His management. It is to your advantage that every person know that there is one higher than him, and that all creation is governed by the law of Allah. This guarantees that you live among them in safety. So it is good for us that God be "there is nothing like unto Him," and that He, glory be to Him, be exalted above everything.

When you declare Allah free of imperfection, you must not declare Him free of imperfection in isolation, but coupled with praise: ﴿and glorify Him with His praise...﴾ (al-Furqan 25:58). So you praise Him for being One, having no partner and no equal, and there being nothing like unto Him. Under the shade of this belief, the strong cannot oppress the weak, nor the rich the poor... etc.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And sufficient is He as Knower of the sins of His servants﴾ (al-Furqan 25:58). We say: "So-and-so suffices you," meaning you have no need of anyone else, as when we say, "Allah is sufficient for you" (hasbuka Allah), meaning He suffices you from needing anyone else, because He gives you everything you need and keeps evil away from you, even if you think it good for you.

Almighty Allah sets up for you a "control" (kontrol) that regulates your life and guarantees your safety. Therefore, when you call upon Allah and He does not respond to you, do not think that Allah is employed by you; He must answer what you want. Rather, He is your Lord and the guardian of your affairs, so He chooses for you what is suitable for you, and bestows upon you the good, even if you see it otherwise.

We have given an example of this matter: the mother who frequently prays against her child. How would it be if Allah answered her? So it is from the mercy of Allah toward her that He returns her prayer and withholds its answer; thus withholding the answer is itself an answer.

﴿And sufficient is He as Knower of the sins of His servants﴾ (al-Furqan 25:58). The meaning: if you rely upon the Living One who does not die, the effect of this reliance is that He protects you from the sins of the servants, for He alone knows their sins and knows even what passes through their souls.

Did not the Truth say to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conferring, then they return to what they were forbidden, and confer together in sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you, and they say within themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" Sufficient for them is Hell; they will burn therein, and wretched is the destination.﴾ (al-Mujadila 58:8)

So the saying within themselves had not yet come out, yet Allah informed him of it. It is as if Almighty Allah reassures His Messenger: however they conspire against you, however they plot for you, and however the hosts of mankind and jinn unite against you, be at peace, for your Lord knows the sins which you may not perceive, and you have no means to repel them. It suffices you that Allah knows the sins of your enemies.

﴿And they plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of plotters﴾ (al-Anfal 8:30).

Al-khabir (the All-Aware, the Expert) is the One who knows the hidden aspects of matters. Even in the important worldly affairs we say: we summon the expert for them, because the ordinary specialist cannot manage them.

In another place, He, exalted be He, says: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾ (al-Mulk 67:14)

Then Almighty Allah transports us to a cosmic sign, added to the preceding signs. The purpose of mentioning further cosmic signs is that perhaps they will meet a tenderness of heart and an attraction of feelings, so that they incline the creation toward the Creator and turn attention to Him, glory be to Him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 59:

﴿Who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then settled upon the Throne, the Most Merciful; so ask about Him one who is informed.﴾

Some people think that creating the heavens and the earth is an easy matter, and that the creation of man is greater than it. But the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind...﴾ (40:57).

Man is created by God, and he may die after a day or after a hundred years, and sicknesses may afflict him during his life. As for the heavens and the earth, God Most High created them with precise engineering and laws that do not fail or break down as time passes over them. It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, is saying to man: These heavens and this earth are My creation and My craftsmanship; if you reflect upon them and contemplate them, you will find them greater than your own creation.

As for His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿in six days...﴾ (25:59): We have already discussed this question and said: the majority of the verses of the Qur'an indicate that creation was completed in a period of six days, except for one surah whose verses suggest that creation took place in eight days, and it is Surah Fussilat, where the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days, and you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. He placed firm mountains upon it, blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: Come, willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly. So He completed them as seven heavens in two days, and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as a guard. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ (41:9-12)

The total of these is eight days. Every summary is subject to detailed explanation, except that the detail of the number returns to the summary. How? 

The Truth, glorified is He, speaks here of the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days. Then He spoke of the creation of the earth in two days, and placing firm mountains upon it, blessing it, and measuring therein its sustenance in four days. So these four days are a completion of the creation of the earth; they are a completion of the two days, as if He said: in the completion of four days. So the earth was in two days, and the remainder completes the four. As you say: I travelled to Tanta in an hour, and to Alexandria in two hours, meaning that the first hour to Tanta is included in them; so the two days are part of the four days.

But how do we measure this day? God addresses us with the day that we know and whose meaning we understand. So the meaning is: in six of your days which you know.

Otherwise, if what was meant were a day we do not know, it would have no meaning for us, because we would not understand it.

One may say: how does creation take all this period when God, blessed and exalted is He, creates by "Be," and "Be" requires no time? They said: there is a difference between the process of creation and what the created thing needs in its own essence.

For example, if you want to make a cup of yogurt, you bring milk, for instance, and put on it the well-known yogurt culture taken from a rich yogurt made earlier, and place it at a certain temperature. After this process you have indeed made the yogurt, but can you eat from it immediately upon finishing its making? No; rather you must leave it for several hours so that its elements interact. Would you then say: I made the yogurt in several hours, for example?

Likewise, when you go to the tailor to have a garment tailored, he tells you: our appointment is after a month. Does sewing the garment take a month? No; rather its duration with him is a month.

So the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, acts and creates without treatment, and therefore without time, because He, glorified is He, says to a thing: "Be," and it is.

As for His saying, glorified is He, ﴿then settled upon the Throne...﴾ (25:59): We have already discussed this question. "Istawa" means: ascended, rose, exalted, and sat. We exalt God, Most High, above a settling resembling the settling of His creatures.

The settling here is a symbol of the complete accomplishment of the matter, by what we know from the custom of kings in sitting on the throne's seat, when their affair is accomplished and becomes firmly established.

And ﴿the Most Merciful...﴾ (25:59): is evidence that the whole question of creation revolves within the framework of mercy. ﴿So ask about Him one who is informed﴾ (25:59): because He, glorified is He, created the heavens and the earth and created us, and yet we do not know how this creation was done. We will not be able to stand upon the details of this creation unless the Creator informs us of it; otherwise it is a matter we did not witness, so how can we delve into it? Like one who says: the earth was a piece of the sun, then it separated from it as the sun rotated... and so on, these sayings.

Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, warns us against listening to such theories, because the question of creation is never subject to experimental science. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, nor did I take misleading ones as helpers﴾ (18:51).

So there will be in the universe misleaders who tell people such sayings about creation, and claim by them that they are scholars who know what people do not know. Beware of them: they did not witness the process of creation, and they were not helpers to God so as to be informed of the details of creation.

Therefore these sayings about the creation of man and the creation of the heavens and earth stand as evidence for the truth of this verse. So what is the position of this verse, then, if these sayings did not exist?

An example of this is those who enjoy being fanatical for the Noble Qur'an against the Prophetic hadith. One of them says to you: Tell me about the Qur'an. Glory be to God! Are you fanatical for the Qur'an against the Messenger who conveyed the Qur'an to you, and you only knew the Qur'an through him? That is, this "son of the Lord" recognizes only the Qur'an. We say to such a one who attacks the Prophetic hadith: You prayed Maghrib as three rak'ahs, so where is that in the Qur'an?

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Soon a man will be reclining on his couch, relating a hadith from me, and he will say: Between us and you is the Book of God. Whatever we find in it lawful, we make lawful, and whatever is unlawful there, we make unlawful. But what the Messenger of God made unlawful is like what God made unlawful."

Why? Because I tell you, from the inner meaning of God's saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it...﴾ (59:7).

By God, if no one were now to say this saying, what would be the position of this hadith, and how could we understand it? This hadith has exposed them and made clear the stupidity they hold; they could, after knowing the Messenger of God's hadith, have refrained from fanaticism for the Qur'an against the Prophetic hadith, and then the hadith would have been without meaning for them. But far-fetched is that.

Returning to our subject, while we are speaking about the creation of the heavens and the creation of the earth, and the settling of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, upon the Throne, these two matters are not asked about except of God: ﴿so ask about Him one who is informed﴾ (25:59), because He alone knows the hidden matters, and these are matters no one has witnessed so as to inform you of them.

The word "sa'ala" (asked): a person does not ask about a thing except when he is ignorant of it, and asking has stages. You may be ignorant of a thing and not care about it, and not wish to know it; you are one among those who do not know. And you may be ignorant of a thing but care about it, so you ask about it because of your concern for it. Thus once we say: "as'al bihi" (ask by/with it), and once we say: "as'al 'anhu" (ask about it).

The meaning: ask with concern for it, i.e., the cause of your concern for it: ask about it one who is informed, so that he may give you and tell you what you want, for He alone knows the hidden matters and their details, and He has the report of the creation of the heavens and the creation of the earth, and knows the matter of settling upon the Throne. Therefore, if you ask about these two matters, ask none but one who is informed.

As for those who said regarding His saying, ﴿so ask about Him one who is informed﴾ (25:59), that is: of those who know speech about God from the People of the Book, we say: there is no harm, because it will ultimately return to God, Most High.

1 Al-Dukhan (smoke): is applied to gases rising above fire that have not completed burning, and it may be applied to vapour and similar rising gases. What is meant is that the materials of the stars were in a gaseous state like smoke, then the heavens were created from them. (Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/224).
2 I.e., helpers and supporters. God Most High also said: ﴿He said: We will strengthen your arm through your brother...﴾ (28:35), i.e., We will strengthen you through him, by way of metonymy, since strengthening the arm is strengthening the whole person. (Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/24).
3 Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/132), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2664), Ibn Majah in his Sunan (12), and al-Daraqutni (4/286) in his Sunan; the wording is that of al-Daraqutni.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 60:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate yourselves to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate ourselves to what you command us?" And it increases them in aversion.﴾

We observe that the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, when He mentioned the attribute that obliges submission to Him, glorified is He, did not say, for example: "Prostrate yourselves to Allah." Rather, He said: ﴿Prostrate yourselves to the Most Merciful...﴾ (al-Furqan 60), and brought the attribute through which His mercy reaches you. So it is obligatory that you obey and submit to Him. As we said previously: make your obedience to one whom you cannot do without, and make your submission to One whose dominion you cannot leave.

﴿And what is the Most Merciful...﴾ (al-Furqan 60): as if they do not know this word; they know only "Rahman of al-Yamama" (Musaylima's name for the god he claimed).

Their saying: ﴿Shall we prostrate ourselves to what you command us...﴾ (al-Furqan 60) is evidence that the refusal to prostrate is not directed at the one to whom prostration is made, but at the one who commands prostration. Like those who previously said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a man of importance from the two towns?﴾ (al-Zukhruf 31). As if, were Allah to command them to prostrate, they would prostrate; but how can the command come from the Messenger in particular? And what is his distinction over them that he should command them? Therefore He said after it: ﴿And it increases them in aversion﴾ (al-Furqan 60). And "nufur" (aversion) is: separating oneself from a thing with dislike.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 61:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Blessed is He who has placed in the sky constellations (buruj), and has placed therein a lamp and a luminous moon.﴾

The discourse returns once more to a cosmic sign, because the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, alternates between a verse that asks something of them and another that draws their attention to the power and greatness of God. This shows the extent of their obstinacy, stubbornness and defiance, and the eagerness of the Truth, glory be to Him, to turn them towards Himself and to take them by the hand to His presence, exalted is He.

Had He wished, glory be to Him, He could have recited the cosmic signs all at once and the verses of denial all at once, but He pairs these with those so that the lesson may pierce more deeply into the hearts of the believers.

We have said: ﴿Blessed...﴾ (61, al-Furqan): meaning, He is exalted, His station is lofty, and His goodness and blessing are great. Buruj is the plural of burj (tower), which is a strong, lofty fortress that no one can storm. Today they apply it to tall buildings, and say: Burj al-Ma'adi, Burj al-Nil, etc. From the same root is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿By the sky holding the constellations (dhat al-buruj)﴾ (1, al-Buruj).

And His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers built high...﴾ (78, al-Nisa').

And the buruj are stations in the sky by which people reckon times, and link them to fortunes. You will find one of them, as soon as he opens the morning newspaper, looking at the section "Your Horoscope Today." The verses indicate that God made these constellations to ease people's affairs of reckoning.

As He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿The sun and the moon are by reckoning﴾ (5, al-Rahman).

And the Exalted said: ﴿And the sun and the moon as a reckoning...﴾ (96, al-An'am).

That is: by them the times are reckoned. The sun gives you the daily and nightly times, and the moon guides you to the beginning of each month, because it appears in a specific form and a particular manner which clarifies for you the start, middle and end of the month. Then the sun, through the shadow, gives you the reckoning of the fractions of time.

It is well known that there are twelve constellations in the sky, which the poet gathered in his verse: "The Ram, the Bull, the Twins, the Crab, the Lion, the Virgin, the Scales, the Scorpion, the Archer, the Goat, the Water-bearer, and the Fish, which contain what we know of the Syrian nation." They are: Aries (al-Hamal), Taurus (al-Thawr), Gemini (al-Jawza'), Cancer (al-Saratan), Leo (al-Asad), Virgo (al-Sunbula), Libra (al-Mizan), Scorpio (al-'Aqrab), Sagittarius (al-Qaws), Capricorn (al-Jady), Aquarius (al-Dalw), and Pisces (al-Hut). The first is al-Hamal and the last is al-Hut, and each constellation begins on the 21st of the month and ends on the 20th.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And has placed therein a lamp and a luminous moon﴾ (61, al-Furqan). The siraj is the lamp that we kindle to give heat and self-generated light, and what is meant here is the sun, because its light is self-generated from it, and so is its heat. This is unlike the moon, which shines by means of rays reflected from its surface, so its illumination is not self-generated. For this reason they call the light of the moon "the gentle light," because it is light without heat.

Remarkably, the surface of the moon, as they have found it, is stone; and when they took a stone from it to conduct their researches on it, did the moon's light diminish? No, because its complete disc is what reflects the sun's light to us, and when you take a stone from it, it reflects to you what lies beneath it of the sun's rays.

In another place, the Truth, glory be to Him, clarifies this matter, saying: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light...﴾ (5, Yunus). So the radiance (diya') is that which comes from the star itself, self-generated, while the light (nur) is the reflection of light off another body, so it is not self-generated.

1 Buruj: the positions of the stars in the sky and their stations. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/61).

Then the Exalted says:

﴿And it is He who made the night and the day in succession for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be grateful.﴾

We know that the night is the sun's withdrawal from one half of the earthly globe, and the day is the sun's facing of the other half, and that night and day alternate, ﴿in succession﴾ (al-Furqan): the night comes and is followed by the day, each one behind the other. This matter is clear to us now. But how did it begin when God Most High created the first creation? At that time, was the sun facing the earth or turned away from it?

If the Exalted created the sun facing the earth, then day is first, and then the sun sets and night comes to succeed the day; day was not preceded by night. Likewise, if at the creation the sun was not facing the earth, then night is first and is not preceded by day. In either case one of them would not be in succession to the other, and we want the verse to apply to both.

Therefore, they must have been in succession from the very first creation. This is because the earth, as we know, and there is no longer any doubt about this matter, is spherical; and when God, blessed and exalted, created the sun and the moon in the first creation, the part facing the sun was day and the part facing the moon was night; then the motion of the cosmos turns, and one succeeds the other from the beginning.

This theory holds only if we say the earth is spherical, and this is indicated by His saying: ﴿Nor can the night outstrip the day...﴾ (Ya-Sin, 40).

The meaning also includes: nor can the day outstrip the night. But the night is mentioned because they used to believe that the night was created first, why? Because for them the day is established by its night, as happens for example in fasting. Do you fast first during the day and then see the crescent at night? Rather, you see the crescent at night first, so it is as if Ramadan begins its day with its night.

Since this is the case, the night precedes the day in their view; this is a matter they believe and accept, and the Qur'an addressed them on the basis of this belief: You believe that the night precedes the day, meaning the day does not precede the night; yes, but know also that the night does not precede the day. So the conclusion: neither does the night precede the day, nor does the day precede the night.

And if we said the earth is flat, this statement would not hold for us.

But which night? And which day? My day, or the day of the one opposite me? Every moment, a day is being born and a night begins somewhere, because when the sun sets for me it rises on others, and my noon coincides with someone else's afternoon, or sunset, or night prayer.

Thus all of time is time, and this difference in times means that the call to prayer, "Allahu akbar," is sounded throughout all time; God Most High is worshipped at every hour and in every age: you say "Allahu akbar," and another says "I bear witness that there is no god but God..." and so on.

And if the Exalted created the night for rest and sleep and the day for striving and work, then this is the general rule but it is not a fixed matter: when the interests of people conflict with this matter, some people's nature of work requires them to work at night, such as bakers, guards, nurses, etc.

These are permitted to work at night and rest by day. And if these had no outlet, we would say that this speech contradicts the cosmic order of creation; therefore, the Exalted says in another verse: ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day...﴾ (al-Rum, 23), so this verse takes into account the circumstances of those who are compelled to work at night and rest by day.

As for His saying: ﴿for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be grateful﴾ (al-Furqan): meaning: O you whom the work of your day has occupied from remembering your Lord, seize the opportunity of the night; and O you whom the sleep of the night has occupied from remembering your Lord, seize the opportunity of the day. This is like the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed God extends His hand by night so that the one who sinned by day may repent, and He extends His hand by day so that the one who sinned by night may repent" (1).

Whoever misses something in his night should make it up in his day, and whoever misses something in his day should make it up in his night. And if God Most High extends His hand by night and extends His hand by day, and both continue, this means that His hand is always extended.

The meaning of ﴿wishes to remember...﴾ (al-Furqan) is: he reflects and contemplates the signs of God, by night and by day, as if he wishes to catch for God blessings for which to thank Him, unlike the heedless one who pays no attention to any of this. It is among God's favors upon us that He alerts us to these blessings and draws our attention to them, because we are a people of heedlessness.

As for His saying: ﴿or wishes to be grateful﴾ (al-Furqan): that is, thankfulness; it is an intensive form of gratitude.

(1) Narrated by Imam Muslim in his Sahih (2759) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, and likewise Ahmad in his Musnad (4/395-404).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 25, verse 63:

﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾:

Almighty Allah gives us a picture of true servanthood and a model of those who followed the method. It is as if He—blessed and exalted is He—says to us: Leave aside those who turned away from the way of Allah and denied His Messenger, and look at the attributes of My servants who believed in Me, carried out My judgments, and affirmed My Messenger.

We say: "ʿibād" and "ʿabīd" (servants). The verified view is that "ʿabīd" is the plural of "ʿabd," and that "ʿibād" is the plural of "ʿabbād," like "rijāl," the plural of "rājil" (on foot): ﴿And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot...﴾ (al-Hajj 27). So: "ʿabīd" are not "ʿibād."

We have previously discussed the difference between the ʿabīd and the ʿibād. All of us are servants of Allah the Exalted: the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient. Whatever befalls a person in his life which he cannot repel, though he hates it, he is subdued by it. The disbelieving servant who rebelled against faith in Allah, rebelled against affirming the Messenger, and rebelled against the judgments of Allah, so did not act upon them—

So, after he has become accustomed to rebellion, can he rebel against sickness if it befalls him? Or can he rebel against death if it arrives at his doorstep? Thus, you are a servant despite yourself. We are all servants in that which we are compelled to; then, after that, we have a space of choice.

As for the believer, he has stepped out of the choice that Allah granted him, to believe or to disbelieve, and has relinquished it to the will of his Lord, so he deserves to be among the servants of Allah: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful...﴾ (al-Furqan 63). So although we are servants, we are masters, because we are servants of the Most Merciful. Therefore, the ground of Allah's honouring His Messenger ﷺ in the Night Journey was his servanthood to Allah the Exalted, as He said: ﴿Glory be to the One who took His servant by night...﴾ (al-Isra' 1). Servanthood is the cause of elevation.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sincerely devoted himself to servanthood, he attained this nearness which no human had preceded him to.

Therefore He described the angels as ﴿honoured servants﴾ (al-Anbiya' 26). And by surveying the verses, we find only one verse that seems to contradict this meaning we have stated concerning the meaning of "ʿibād," namely His saying about the Hereafter: ﴿Did you lead astray these My servants?...﴾ (al-Furqan 17).

He says to the misguided "My servants" (ʿibādī), a term that is only used for the obedient. Why? They said: because on the Day of Resurrection no one has choice, so all are servants on that Day, since the choice that distinguishes them has ceased.

The scholars say: from "ʿibād" is derived "ʿibādiyyah" (worship-servitude), and from "ʿabīd" is derived "ʿubūdiyyah" (servanthood/enslavement). ʿIbādiyyah in the ʿibād is that the worshipper obeys the command of Allah and refrains from His prohibitions, desiring His reward in the Hereafter and fearing His punishment there. So ʿibādiyyah came to seek the reward of the Hereafter and avoid its punishment.

As for ʿubūdiyyah, it does not look to the Hereafter; rather, it looks to the fact that Allah the Exalted has preceded His servants with His kindness: bringing them into existence from non-existence, sustaining them from non-existence, nurturing them, and subjecting the cosmos to them. So Allah deserves, by what He has bestowed of kindness, to be obeyed, regardless of recompense in the Hereafter, whether reward or punishment.

As for ʿubūdiyyah, it is: that the servant does not look at the kindness he has received, nor at what is deferred of reward and punishment, but looks at the majesty of Allah, who deserves to be obeyed, even if no kindness had preceded it and even if no reward or punishment were to come afterwards.

Although servanthood is disliked among human beings, as one of the politicians said (2): "When did you enslave people, when their mothers bore them free?" This is because servanthood to humans takes the master's best from his servant, whereas servanthood to Allah the Exalted is might and honour, for the servant takes the best of his Master. It is servanthood of lordship, not servanthood of subjugation.

When you believe in Allah, He gives you the reins. He says to you: If you wish that I remember you, then remember Me. And in the sacred hadith: "Whoever remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs." (3)

And if He—exalted is He—summons you to five prayers in the day and night, that is only so that you may be at ease with your Lord. But you are free to come to Him at any time you wish, without an appointment, and you may determine the start of the meeting, its end, its subject, and so on. The control of the matter is in your hand. Our master, the Messenger of Allah, was taught by Allah: whenever he placed his hand in the hand of one of the Companions to greet him, he would not withdraw his hand until the other was the one who withdrew his hand from the Messenger of Allah's (4). This is one of the courtesies of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He. Therefore: servanthood to Allah is servanthood to the Merciful, not servanthood to the Compeller.

The first thing we notice in this verse is that He—exalted is He—attributed the servants to the Most Merciful, so that we do not think that servanthood to Allah is abasement, and that the Qur'an is the speech of a Lord set on a scale. Then He—exalted is He—mentions the attributes of these servants: their attributes in themselves, their attributes with their society, their attributes with their Lord, and their attributes in elevating society to purity and cleanliness.

As for their selves, a human has two states which are the focus of attention: either seated or walking. We set aside the state of sleep, since it is a time of stillness. As for the state of sitting, movement in it is limited to one's own person, and what matters is the state of movement and walking, and this is the state that deserves attention.

Therefore our Lord—mighty and majestic is He—clarifies for us how to walk, saying: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility...﴾ (al-Furqan 63).

That is: gently and with tranquillity, with softness, without arrogance, pride, or haughtiness. Why? Because walking is what will expose you to meeting diverse societies, and this divine etiquette of walking produces in society a human passage that levels everyone together.

In another place He says on this matter: ﴿And do not turn your cheek away from people, nor walk on the earth exultantly...﴾ (Luqman 18), ﴿Indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, nor will you reach the mountains in height.﴾ (al-Isra' 37).

Tasʿīr al-khadd (turning the cheek) is to incline it out of pride and insolence. Its root, "al-ṣaʿr," is an illness in a camel that affects its neck, so that it walks leaning. Whoever wishes to walk proudly and arrogantly, let him be proud of something intrinsic in himself. Do you have something intrinsic that you can guarantee for yourself or keep?

If you are rich, you may become poor; if you are strong and healthy, sickness may afflict you and confine you to bed; if you are mighty today, you may be humbled tomorrow. So all the causes of pride are not intrinsic to you; rather, they are bestowed by Allah. Why then pride?

Therefore they say in the proverb: "Whoever stitches, stitches on his own hip." But does one stitch on another's hip? The origin of this proverb is that a saddle-maker would bring a boy who worked under him, have him stretch out his leg, place the saddle on his hip, and then begin sewing it. One of them saw this and felt pity for the boy, and said to the man: "He is weak and cannot bear this; if you wish, put it on your own hip." Likewise here: whoever wishes to be proud, let him be proud of something intrinsic in himself, not of something bestowed upon him.

The arrogant person is one upon whose heart a veil has been cast, so he does not turn to his Lord, the Most High, and sees himself as better than all of Allah's creation. Had he kept in mind the greatness of his Lord, he would be ashamed to be arrogant toward Allah's creation; so his arrogance is a proof of his heedlessness of this matter.

Therefore the poet says: "Leave every tyrant to time, for time will straighten the crooked neck." That is: time will show him what straightens his crookedness and humbles his nose.

The meaning of ﴿exultantly﴾ (Luqman 18), "maraḥ," is joy accompanied by insolence. Insolence (baṭar) is to take a blessing and forget the Bestower, to enjoy it while disobeying the One who gave it to you. So what is forbidden is joy accompanied by insolence and denial of the Bestower's favour. As for joy accompanied by gratitude, it is praiseworthy, as He said: ﴿Say: "By the bounty of Allah and His mercy—in that let them rejoice."﴾ (Yunus 58).

In another place He teaches us the etiquette of walking, saying: ﴿And be moderate in your walking and lower your voice...﴾ (Luqman 19).

They said: what is meant by walking "in humility" (hawnan) is the walk in which a person moves naturally, without contriving humility or pride, yet without submissiveness and abasement. Our master ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, when he saw a man walking in a feigned, languid manner, struck him and forbade him from submissiveness and feigned languor in gait. Thus the walk of the believer is moderate: neither proud nor feebly exhausted.

Then the verse speaks of the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful and their relationship with people: ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ (al-Furqan 63). The "jāhil" (ignorant) is the foolish one who does not weigh his words, does not place the word in its proper place, and does not grasp the measures of matters, neither in character nor in manners.

We have previously distinguished between the jāhil and the ummī: the ummī is blank of mind, having no information he believes in, and such a person is easy to persuade of the right. But the jāhil has information that contradicts reality; therefore he takes from you effort in persuading him, because he first needs you to remove the error from his mind, and then to enter the right into his heart.

The meaning is: if the ignorant addresses you, beware of being like him in responding, so that you respond with foolishness as he did to you; rather, address him with courtesy and say ﴿"Peace"﴾ (al-Furqan 63), so as to make him feel the difference between you.

The Truth—blessed and exalted is He—clarifies in another verse the fruit of this etiquette, saying: ﴿Repel evil with that which is better, and then the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ (Fussilat 34).

How beautiful is what Imam al-Shafiʿi said on this meaning: "When the fool speaks, do not answer him; silence is better than his answer. If you answer him, you have relieved him; if you leave him, he dies of vexation." (5)(6)

If the fool grows excessively foolish, overbearing and tyrannical toward you, then you must return aggression with its like, for you have shown forbearance toward him and he did not become humble to you, but took your forbearance for weakness; here you must show him the difference between weakness and nobility of character, as the poet (7) said:

"We forgave the people of Dhuhl and said, 'They are our brothers';
perhaps the days will return them to being like those who were—
Until, when war declared itself and morning came naked,
and nothing remained but enemies, we repaid them as they had repaid us.
We walked the walk of a lion, now at dawn, the lion enraged,
striking in it with humiliation, subjugation, and confrontation,
and stabbing like the mouth of a waterskin at dawn while the skin is full.
In evil there is salvation when kindness will not save you.
And some forbearance in the face of ignorance is submission and abasement."

And Imam ʿAli, may Allah honour his face, said:
"If I am in need of forbearance, I am
sometimes in need of ignorance more than that.
I have a horse bridled with forbearance for forbearance,
and I have a horse saddled with ignorance for ignorance.
So whoever seeks to straighten me, I am straightened;
and whoever seeks to bend me, I am bent."

As for the meaning of ﴿they say, "Peace"﴾ (al-Furqan 63): "they say" here means the peace of disengagement, not the peace of safety that we say in greeting ("Peace be upon you"). So when you encounter one who harms you with speech and transgresses against you with his tongue, you say to him "Peace," meaning the peace of disengagement.

Some scholars hold that the phrase ﴿they say, "Peace"﴾ (al-Furqan 63) here means both meanings: the peace of disengagement and the peace of greeting and safety. So when you show forbearance toward the fool and do not match him, you say to him: "If you persist with me, I will harm you and do such-and-such to you"; thus you have moved from the peace of disengagement to the peace of greeting and safety.

From this is His saying: ﴿And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say, "For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds; peace be upon you; we do not seek the ignorant."﴾ (al-Qasas 55).

Did not Abraham, peace be upon him, say to his uncle Azar when he insisted upon his disbelief: ﴿"Peace be upon you; I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord..."﴾ (Maryam 47).

The meaning is: if you stood before him, he might well transgress against you, and the problem between us would escalate.

Following the verses on the conduct of the servants of the Most Merciful towards themselves and towards people, the discussion now turns to their relationship with their Lord:

﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing.﴾ (25:64)

Spending the night (al-baytutah) takes place at night, when a person returns to his home after the fatigue and exertion of the day, and after having experienced various kinds of God's blessings upon him. When he retires to his resting place, he remembers the blessings of God that were manifest to him that day. These blessings are not inherent in him; rather, they are bestowed upon him by God. Therefore he turns to Him, glorified is He, in gratitude for them, and so he spends the night before God, prostrating and standing.

As He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord...?﴾ (39:9) (Az-Zumar).

And He, glorified is He, said: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night, and at the dawn they would seek forgiveness.﴾ (51:17-18) (Adh-Dhariyat).

But does God ask us not to sleep at night, when He has said in another verse: ﴿And We made your sleep a rest﴾ (78:9) (An-Naba')?

They said: The intended meaning is not standing in prayer the whole night, but a part of it, when you find within yourself the energy for worship, as the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said in addressing the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him:

﴿Stand (in prayer) through the night, except a little, half of it, or reduce it a little, or add to it, and recite the Qur'an in slow, measured recitation.﴾ (73:2-4) (Al-Muzzammil).

To the point that Ibn 'Abbas said: whoever prays two units or more after the 'Isha' prayer is as one who has spent the night before Allah, prostrating and standing. So your Lord wants you to remember Him before you sleep, and to reflect upon His blessings upon you, so that you thank Him for them.

He, glorified is He, mentioned the two states of prostration and standing ﴿prostrating and standing﴾ (25:64) because some people find prostration difficult, while others find prostration easy but standing difficult. So Allah, glorified is He, mentioned both states so that they might be balanced between them.

¹ Al-Asḥar (the dawns): plural of saḥar, which is the last part of the night up to the break of dawn. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/305).
